As a responsible investor, the HKMA has set a target for its Exchange Fund portfolio to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier, as a commitment to its participation in global climate action and the implementation of recommendations from the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures. Looking ahead, the HKMA will continue to incorporate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors into its investment management processes, strive towards the net-zero emissions target, and fully support global climate action efforts. As a responsible and sustainable institution, the HKMA cares not only about its employees but also about the general public and the surrounding environment. We have developed a sustainability roadmap and established climate targets for our own operations as a commitment to our participation in global carbon reduction and climate action. The HKMA will continue to prioritize the reduction of carbon emissions and encourage full employee support in energy conservation and waste reduction. In addition, we will provide further guidance to employees to incorporate sustainability principles into procurement processes. To practice digital transformation and enhance operational flexibility, the HKMA will explore methods to modernize internal systems and applications to further improve work efficiency, while minimizing potential risks that may arise during the digital transformation process as much as possible.

Climate change represents a significant risk facing the financial system. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has been committed to strengthening Hong Kong's financial system to build a greener and more sustainable future, contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks face various impacts from sustainability and climate-related issues in their daily operations. To continue fulfilling their vital role in the financial system and to channel more capital into green and sustainable projects, banks must proactively manage climate risks. As the banking regulator, the HKMA places particular emphasis on building banks' capacity to respond to and manage climate risks, and on accelerating banks' efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economic model. The HKMA also supports banks in enhancing their capabilities to detect environmental crimes and participated in the recently published Hong Kong Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Risk Assessment, which covers areas such as environmental crimes and illegal wildlife trafficking. In 2022, the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS)1 issued the Principles for the Effective Management and Supervision of Climate-Related Financial Risks and responded to frequently asked questions to clarify how the existing Basel framework addresses these risks. In response to these international developments, the HKMA will continue to strive to integrate climate-related factors into its regulatory framework. Following the issuance of Module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" of the "Supervisory Policy Manual" in 2021, the HKMA has maintained communication with banks to exchange views on expectations, progress, and challenges regarding the implementation of relevant regulatory requirements. To further strengthen the supervision of banks' climate risk management, the HKMA has formulated a two-year plan to incorporate climate risk factors into the bank supervisory process, which was communicated to the banking sector in June. As part of the implementation of this two-year plan, the HKMA issued the revised Module SA-1 "Risk-Based Supervisory Regime" of the "Supervisory Policy Manual," enhancing the CAMEL2 rating system by integrating climate risks into the risk-based supervisory process. Concurrently, drawing on lessons learned from the 2021 pilot programme, the HKMA has improved the scenarios and assessment framework for climate risk stress testing. The HKMA has also developed a plan to incorporate the next round of climate risk stress testing into the regulator-led regular stress testing programme, enabling a more comprehensive assessment of the banking sector's resilience under extreme climate scenarios. Under this two-year plan, the HKMA is also strengthening its Green Assessment Framework for banks to reflect the latest developments in sustainability-related issues, including climate risk management and transition planning. At the same time, the HKMA is reviewing the supervisory review process used to assess and monitor banks' capital adequacy and determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, with the aim of encouraging banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks to address risks associated with climate change and the transition to carbon neutrality. Given the increasing prevalence of banks issuing green and sustainable products, the HKMA conducted a thematic review focusing on banks' development and ongoing management of these products. During the thematic review, the HKMA identified several good practices and issued a circular in December to share them with the industry, facilitating banks' gradual enhancement of their climate risk management capabilities. The application of technology can improve data availability and strengthen banks' ability to manage climate risks. The HKMA has begun developing a common platform for banks to assess the impact of physical risks on real estate. Furthermore, together with other central banks and regulators, the HKMA completed a project under the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) Innovation Hub to explore how technology solutions can assist in physical risk assessment. The HKMA also places great importance on promoting sustainable and globally leading anti-money laundering (AML) operational practices; this work employs advanced analytics and regulatory technology (RegTech), supported by fully automated supervisory data collection. Over the past 12 months, the HKMA has streamlined the AML supervisory data collection process to reduce the manpower burden and paper usage for banks. To enhance transparency among financial markets and align green finance policies, the HKMA is collaborating with other financial regulators to establish a local green taxonomy framework. Generally referred to as a green taxonomy, this framework classifies economic activities as green or sustainable, providing a reference for authorities and market participants to determine whether an activity or its related products are genuinely green or sustainable. To this end, the HKMA maintains close contact with the industry and other relevant stakeholders to thoroughly explore the features and challenges of the framework, and is preparing to propose and consult on the framework's structure and core elements in the first half of 2023. Recognizing that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system, the HKMA has incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into its financial risk analysis and research to strengthen current monitoring efforts. In its ongoing monitoring of financial stability risks, the HKMA takes climate change into account and includes analysis of climate-related risks in its various financial stability reports. Through active participation in the Scenario Design and Analysis Working Group under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA assists in further enriching climate scenarios, enabling central banks and regulators to better understand the impacts of climate change on the macroeconomy and finance. In terms of research, the HKMA conducted several applied research projects in 2022, delving into two major topics: greenwashing in the corporate green bond market3 and the role of disclosure in mitigating climate risk exposure4. The findings from these studies assist in formulating policies and regulatory measures to address the impact of climate risks on financial stability. Locally, these studies help strengthen the HKMA's ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate risks on financial stability. Externally, the HKMA has shared research outcomes with a wide range of stakeholders through various channels, including international central bank research seminars and its own "Semi-Annual Report on Currency and Financial Stability." The HKMA's "Liquidity Arrangement Framework" is a collateralized standby liquidity facility that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The HKMA is studying the incorporation of sustainability considerations into the assessment of eligible collateral under this framework. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risks and promoting sustainable finance as the mainstream. Through such participation, the HKMA helps facilitate policy dialogue between international and regional actors on addressing climate change and its impact on financial stability, drawing insights to strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong's financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as a regional hub for green and sustainable finance, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has intensified efforts to enhance market awareness and engagement, provide necessary infrastructure and drivers, and support international initiatives to align with global standards. The Cross-Bureau Steering Group on Green and Sustainable Finance (Steering Group), co-led by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), is responsible for coordinating the financial sector's response to climate and environmental risks, accelerating the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong, and supporting the government's climate strategy1. The Steering Group's work is primarily guided by its Strategic Plan, which outlines six key focus areas and five action pillars to strengthen Hong Kong's financial ecosystem and co-build a greener and more sustainable future (Figure 1). These pillars include: strengthening climate-related financial risk management to consolidate Hong Kong's status as a global risk management centre; promoting the flow of climate-related information across all levels to facilitate risk management, capital allocation, and investor protection; enhancing relevant skills within the industry and raising public awareness and understanding; encouraging product innovation and research measures to direct capital towards green and sustainable projects; seizing business opportunities from the Mainland to develop Hong Kong as the green finance centre for the Greater Bay Area (GBA); and strengthening regional and international cooperation. Actions taken thus far to advance sustainable finance in Hong Kong: Since its establishment, the Steering Group has made good progress. Current work priorities include skills training and data collection under the Green and Sustainable Finance Centre (see below), the Green Taxonomy (see "Establishing a Green Taxonomy Framework to Facilitate Green Capital Flows" in Chapter 9 "Building a Sustainable Financial System"), climate-related disclosure and sustainable reporting, and opportunities in the carbon market. Specifically, in March, the Steering Group published a preliminary feasibility assessment of opportunities for Hong Kong's carbon market and will support Hong Kong's development as a regional carbon trading centre, including the development of a high-quality international voluntary carbon market and seizing opportunities arising from GBA cooperation. In December, the Steering Group announced a collaboration with CDP2 to enhance data availability in Hong Kong and strengthen sustainability reporting. As part of this collaboration, the two parties developed a climate and environmental risk questionnaire targeting non-listed companies and small and medium enterprises (SMEs), facilitating corporate sustainability reporting while assisting financial institutions in collecting and analysing company-level data for risk assessment and related business decisions. This represents an important step in expanding the Steering Group's data work coverage to include SMEs, a previously hard-to-reach yet vital economic segment. The Steering Group established the Green and Sustainable Finance Centre in July 2021 to coordinate training and policy formulation efforts among financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders, and academic institutions, and to build resources and databases. In the first half of 2022, the Centre launched three repositories focusing on data, training information, and internship opportunities to assist the financial sector and other sectors in accessing data and learning resources related to green and sustainable finance. The resource repository provides data sources for assessing Hong Kong's physical risks. To assist industry talent training, the Centre helped the government launch the "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme" in December, providing subsidies to practitioners, students, and graduates participating in training and skill enhancement related to green and sustainable finance. Other measures to promote skills training include the launch of the "Sustainable Finance Internship Scheme" to create more internship opportunities for students, and the development of a new module on "Green and Sustainable Finance" under the HKMA's "Banking Professional Qualifications Framework" for banking practitioners3. "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme" The HKMA has also actively supported the development of green and sustainable finance in the region. In November 2020, the International Finance Corporation (IFC) and the HKMA launched the "Green Banking Alliance"4, bringing together regional financial institutions, banking industry organisations, research institutions, and fintech providers to jointly develop a collaborative platform for green commercial banking. The Alliance aims to enable commercial banks and other financial institutions to fully realise their potential, mainstream green finance as a core business, and promote the financial sector's participation in global climate change-related activities. It operates as a one-stop platform for mutual learning, providing financial institutions with the necessary knowledge, tools, and information to formulate their own green finance roadmaps and transform into credible green financial institutions. It gathers green finance leaders, connects green financial institutions from different emerging markets to facilitate communication and explore frontier issues, and advances the global green finance agenda to unlock endless green and climate-related investment opportunities. In June, five leading global financial institutions5 became cornerstone members of the Alliance, working closely with the IFC and the HKMA to encourage clients to adopt green strategies, promote best practices in green products and services, and release new business opportunities, thereby contributing to the green economic transition. Additionally, three global partners and one knowledge partner6 committed in 2022 to provide climate expertise in areas such as innovation, standardisation, and academic research. Details of the Alliance and its member structure are available on the relevant webpage (English version): Cornerstone Members; IFC and HKMA sign Memorandum of Understanding. On another front, since March 2021, the Alliance has held 18 training sessions and roundtable meetings, attracting over 6,000 participants from across the Asia-Pacific, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Americas. Furthermore, in June 2022, the Alliance, in collaboration with the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and Financial Research Centre (Research Centre)7, published its first frontier research report titled "Climate Risk: Definitions, Measurement, Current Practices and Regulation". The HKMA has consistently promoted the issuance of green and sustainable debt and cultivated a local ecosystem of related professional services. In 2022, the total amount of green and sustainable debt issued in Hong Kong (including bonds and loans) reached US$80.5 billion, a 42% increase. +42% Green and Sustainable Debt Issuance (US$80.5 billion). To demonstrate the government's determination to address climate change, promote green finance, and strive to develop Hong Kong into a more sustainable and livable city, the government launched the "Government Green Bond Programme" in 2018, with the HKMA assisting in the implementation of related green bond issuances. To date, the government has issued green institutional and retail bonds equivalent to nearly US$16 billion, with proceeds allocated to over 40 green government projects, including green buildings, waste management and recycling, energy efficiency, and energy conservation. To enhance transparency and accountability, the government publishes an annual "Green Bond Report" detailing the allocation of proceeds and expected environmental benefits. To enable citizens to participate in Hong Kong's sustainable development through investment and share in the resulting benefits, the first tranche of green retail bonds worth HK$20 billion was issued in May, receiving enthusiastic public support and becoming the largest green retail bond issuance globally at the time. This issuance also expanded the range of green and sustainable financial products in Hong Kong, consolidating its status as the premier green finance hub in the region and internationally. The government continued its regular issuance of green institutional bonds in the 2022-23 financial year and issued green bonds equivalent to US$5.75 billion in January 2023. This three-currency issuance covered USD, EUR, and RMB, with tenors ranging from 2 to 30 years, continuing to provide an important benchmark for potential issuers in Hong Kong and the region. The issuance was well-received by the global investment community and successfully attracted new investors who had not participated in previous government green bond issuances, reflecting investor confidence in Hong Kong's long-term credit standing and economic fundamentals. In response to investor demand, the government doubled the issuance amount of RMB bonds to RMB 10 billion. The share of international investors and Mainland investors participating via the Bond Connect "Southbound" mechanism also increased, demonstrating Hong Kong's role as the premier offshore RMB business hub and further consolidating its leadership as an international financial centre. The HKMA also assisted the government in issuing tokenised institutional green bonds in February 2023 to test the use of distributed ledger technology for bond issuance and settlement. These are the world's first tokenised green bonds issued by a government. This primary issuance settled on a private blockchain network on a T+1 basis, with subsequent processes (including coupon payments, secondary market trading and settlement, and maturity redemption) also digitised. This government issuance experience can serve as a reference for market participants interested in similar bond issuances in the future. To provide the industry with credible and convenient market information, the HKMA continues to collaborate with the Climate Bonds Initiative and the International Capital Market Association (ICMA) to publish annual reports on Hong Kong's and the region's green debt markets respectively. ICMA's report shows that in 2022, Hong Kong became the largest hub in Asia for arranging the issuance of international green and sustainable bonds, with a total of US$27.8 billion arranged through Hong Kong, accounting for more than one-third of the regional total. Largest Hub in Asia for Arranging International Green and Sustainable Bonds: US$27.8 billion. Following its first issuance in 2021, the Shenzhen Municipal Government issued another RMB 5 billion of offshore local government bonds in Hong Kong in November 2022, including RMB 2.6 billion in green and blue bonds8. In the same month, the Hainan Provincial Government also issued its first RMB 5 billion of offshore bonds in Hong Kong, including blue and sustainable bonds. These bond issuance activities repeatedly highlight Hong Kong's unique role in facilitating the flow of green and sustainable capital between the Mainland and the rest of the world, as well as its enduring status as the region's premier fundraising platform. The HKMA continues to promote and implement the "Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme" launched in 2021, using it to attract more relevant professional service providers (including financial institutions, green advisory firms, and external review bodies) to establish and expand their businesses in Hong Kong. The scheme has been widely welcomed by the industry. As of the end of 2022, the scheme has covered pre-issuance, post-issuance, or both external review service expenditures for over 180 green and sustainable debt issuers, helping issuers ensure and demonstrate strict adherence to market best practices and international standards. From March, the scheme was optimised by lowering the minimum loan amount threshold for applying for external review fee subsidies from HK$200 million to HK$100 million, helping smaller enterprises access green financing. Following the successful proof of concept for tokenised retail green bonds under Project Genesis in 2021, the HKMA and the Bank for International Settlements Innovation Hub Hong Kong Centre collaborated again under Genesis 2.0 to explore the technical feasibility of digital carbon forwards (also known as Mitigation Outcome Interests, or MOIs), thereby enhancing the transparency, objectivity, and environmental elements of the green bond market. The project was completed in October 2022, successfully developing two prototypes that use blockchain and other related technologies to track, deliver, and transfer digital MOIs.

As one of the world's largest asset owners and managers, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) plays a pivotal role in promoting green and sustainable finance to support the global climate change agenda. The HKMA is also a pioneer in responsible investment, having led investments in green and sustainable assets as early as 2015. It requires its external investment managers to adopt the Stewardship Code issued by the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) and to integrate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors into the investment management of the Exchange Fund (EF). Adhering to the principle of "capital preservation first, long-term appreciation second," the HKMA invests prudently, believing that prioritizing ESG factors can unlock long-term sustainable value for investments and mitigate related risks. In the face of increasingly severe climate change challenges, the HKMA continues to advance on its responsible investment journey, including setting a "Net Zero by 2050" target in 2022 and optimizing risk management strategies to enhance the resilience of its asset portfolio, thereby seeking more favorable risk-adjusted long-term returns for the EF. The HKMA also actively participates in building a green and sustainable finance ecosystem, collaborating with like-minded investors and regulators to promote responsible investment, and working with international organizations to develop ESG investment standards. Transparency of climate-related information plays a crucial role in managing climate risks. To fulfill its commitment to the Glasgow Declaration issued by the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) at the 2021 UN Climate Change Conference and to green the global financial system, the HKMA has made climate-related disclosures regarding the EF in accordance with the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) under the Financial Stability Board.a. FCLTGlobal — Focusing Capital on the Long Termb. PRI — Principles for Responsible Investmentc. NGFS — Network for Greening the Financial Systemd. TCFD — Task Force on Climate-related Financial DisclosuresThe Exchange Fund Advisory Committee (EFAC), chaired by the Financial Secretary, establishes the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office (EFIO) in the investment management of the EF. The primary guiding principle is to prioritize ESG investments for the HKMA that offer risk-adjusted long-term returns comparable to other options, thereby aligning with the EF's investment objectives. Details of the HKMA's responsible investment framework are available on the HKMA website.The Investment Committee, a sub-committee of EFAC chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for overseeing ESG and climate-related risks associated with EF investment projects. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management policies, and monitors the progress of integrating ESG factors into investments and the EF's overall ESG status through regular meeting reports from the Risk Management and Surveillance Division of the EFIO. As shown in Illustration 1, the ESG Committee established under the EFIO, chaired by the Chief Risk Officer, is responsible for coordinating and monitoring various ESG initiatives within the EFIO. Proposals discussed and work progress at each ESG Committee meeting are reported to the Chief Executive of the EFIO.**Oversight and Governance Structure for Responsible Investment**The dedicated task force within the Risk Management and Surveillance Division works closely with various investment teams of the EFIO to integrate ESG factors and assists the EFIO senior management in managing ESG and climate-related risks and opportunities across various investment projects:**Public Market Investments:** The Credit, Regulatory and Surveillance Committee, composed of EFIO senior management, monitors the ESG status of the fixed income portfolio through regular reports from the Risk Management and Surveillance Division. Additionally, the Risk Management and Surveillance Division participates from an ESG perspective in the selection, appointment, and monitoring processes of external investment managers for the equity portfolio (see the section "Striving for Proactive Stewardship" under "Risk Management" on page 27).**Private Market Investments:** The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers ESG-related assessments made by the Risk Management and Surveillance Division and the private market investment team for each investment proposal.**Concrete Evidence**Concrete evidence continues to show that the impacts of climate change and related risks are significant. According to the latest report by the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), even assuming full implementation of the published "Nationally Determined Contributions" (NDCs) by all regions, global temperature rise by 2100 is estimated to reach 2.1 to 2.4 degrees Celsius, making it difficult to achieve the Paris Agreement's goal of limiting global average temperature rise to well below 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. If regions adopt more aggressive policy measures to narrow the temperature gap, the resulting transition risks, combined with market repricing of assets based on expected future trends and inherent physical risks, will intensify pressure on asset valuations.Given updates to global warming trajectories and model assumptions, the HKMA, leveraging the expertise of external consultants, has further assessed the resilience of the EF "portfolio" under a "Rapid Transition" scenario (Illustration 2), building upon scenarios evaluated in 2021. The "Rapid Transition" scenario incorporates higher transition risk factors in the short, medium, and long terms. It assumes that policy changes and technological developments jointly drive a rapid decline in carbon emissions, while simultaneous disinvestment in various assets occurs to maintain an average temperature rise of within 1.5 degrees Celsius by 2100. This scenario largely aligns with the "Orderly" scenario recommended by the NGFS for forward-looking climate impact assessments.The "portfolio" remains resilient in the medium to long term, as a larger proportion of its asset allocation consists of sovereign bonds with lower sensitivity to transition impacts. Sector distribution is key. Low-carbon power and renewable energy assets can benefit from such transitions. Transition risks and asset repricing may cause short-term shocks to performance, particularly for equity assets. Overall, the "portfolio" will face increasingly severe impacts from physical risks that gradually materialize over time. The energy and traditional utilities sectors remain the most vulnerable.Like other modeling approaches, climate scenario analysis has its limitations. The analysis is based on market benchmark sector distributions at the strategic asset allocation level and does not account for the effects of actively selecting specific securities within a sector. Deeper research reveals that investment projects within the "portfolio" are generally more resilient to transition shocks or subject to less severe impacts compared to the market benchmarks of strategic asset allocation. This result reaffirms that the HKMA's responsible investment, focused on combating climate change, can enhance portfolio resilience.Climate change trajectories remain uncertain, and scenario analysis methods will continue to evolve with improvements in data quality and policy development. The HKMA will regularly review relevant scenarios and optimize assessments to more clearly confirm the EF's resilience against climate change. As a long-term investor, the HKMA fully understands the risks and opportunities brought by climate change. It is committed to further expanding sustainable investments and seizing opportunities related to climate transition, mitigating climate risks, and enhancing long-term portfolio returns.In 2022, maintaining positive momentum, the HKMA increased its holdings of green, social, and sustainable bonds by another 50%. In equity investments, the HKMA invested in actively managed equity portfolios with a governance theme and adopted a decarbonization strategy favoring low-carbon companies for its passive equity portfolios. Furthermore, the HKMA is exploring with the dedicated partner of the EF "Long-Term Growth Portfolio" the establishment of a dedicated private equity portfolio to promote green and sustainable development in the Asia region (Illustration 3).**Illustration 3: Continuously Implementing Measures to Increase ESG Investments**The HKMA has invested in a pan-African wind farm operator. In addition to producing clean energy, this operator places high importance on social factors and biodiversity. Before the wind farm was established, local villagers used poison baits to prevent predatory animals from hunting their livestock, inadvertently endangering certain vulture species listed as endangered. Livestock constitutes important property for local villagers. To assist villagers in protecting their livestock, the operator constructed livestock shelters within the wind farm to protect animals from natural predators. Additionally, the operator employs a bird monitoring team to issue warnings when vultures are attracted by animal carcasses left behind by predators, allowing wind turbines to be shut down to prevent vultures from being struck by blades. Reducing livestock predation creates a win-win situation: it safeguards villagers' livelihoods on one hand, and reduces vulture fatalities caused by wind turbines on the other, thereby protecting endangered species.Good ESG practices can bring more business opportunities and open up new revenue streams for companies; the following supply chain-related operation serves as an example. The investee company is a comprehensive logistics and warehousing operator in mainland China, specializing in cold-chain pharmaceuticals, chemical products, and high-end consumer goods logistics services. Facing continuously rising ESG operational standards, primarily driven by multinational corporate clients requiring their service providers to meet high decarbonization targets aligned with the Paris Agreement, the company hired external consultants to assist in formulating a "Three-Year ESG Plan" to reduce carbon emission density by 50% by 2030 or earlier. This comprehensive decarbonization plan yielded significant results as early as 2021. The aforementioned ESG measures enabled the company to receive the "Low-Carbon Green Management Case" award from the China Federation of Logistics & Purchasing. These achievements and recognitions have allowed the company to secure numerous business opportunities from multinational clients in the consumer and chemical product sectors that particularly value ESG practices.The growth of ESG investment is closely linked to the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem. The HKMA actively collaborates with like-minded investors and partners to promote responsible investment and enhance industry capabilities. In 2022, the HKMA successfully hosted the 4th Annual ESG Workshop, exchanging best ESG practices with nine participating private market institutions (including general partners, limited partners, and corporations), and promoting sustainable investment opportunities in the Asia-Pacific region and the Greater Bay Area. In the public market, the HKMA has urged trading partners (primarily investment banks) to expand their ESG personnel and research capabilities, particularly in Hong Kong.Mr. David Li, Chief Executive of the EFIO, delivered the opening speech at the 2022 HKMA ESG Workshop.At the international level, the HKMA actively participates in developing industry ESG investment standards and practices: As one of the earliest central bank signatories to the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI), the HKMA participates in joint actions coordinated by the PRI to develop a standardized responsible investment due diligence questionnaire for private equity and venture capital investments, assisting private market investors in conducting ESG assessments of general partners and investment proposals. The HKMA participates in multiple working groups to support FCLTGlobal's research, which aims to explore market best practices for long-term portfolios and decarbonizing private assets, as well as their application to long-term investors. As a member of the NGFS and a supporter of the TCFD, the HKMA contributed to the NGFS's "Central Bank Climate-related Disclosures Guidance" to demonstrate its determination to adopt good ESG practices. The HKMA also leads a working group under the NGFS's "Central Bank Net Zero" working group to participate in formulating sustainable and responsible investment policies for the central banking sector. The HKMA continues to participate in various industry forums and lectures to share insights on responsible investment and climate change strategies.Ms. Carrie Lau, Chief Risk Officer of the EFIO (center), spoke at the ESG Investment Opportunities Sharing Session.Building internal capacity is crucial for continuing the ESG journey. In addition to encouraging employees to pursue relevant courses and qualifications in sustainability, the HKMA has drawn upon relevant knowledge and practical experience from the process where external consultants provided recommendations on industry best practices for portfolio climate transition in 2021. On the other hand, the HKMA utilizes ESG data compiled by reputable external information providers to supplement its continuous analysis of the asset portfolio, helping to consolidate the EF's ESG resilience.

The HKMA is committed to reducing its own carbon footprint with the aim of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier, thereby contributing to Hong Kong's overall climate goals. While actively promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA also fulfills its commitments to caring for employee well-being, encouraging financial inclusion, and upholding social responsibility. The HKMA is dedicated to conducting its daily operations in a responsible and sustainable manner. To this end, the HKMA practices sustainability principles under three pillars: environment, employees, and social responsibility (Diagram 1). The Institutional Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee is responsible for leading the HKMA in formulating and implementing its sustainability strategy. Chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, the Committee comprises three Deputy Chief Executives and representatives from the Risk Management and Surveillance Department and the Institutional Development and Operations Department; it submits regular reports to the Governance Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee. Under the leadership of this Committee, various teams and working groups are responsible for planning and executing measures within their respective domains. In 2022, the Institutional Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee approved the HKMA's operational climate targets and reviewed the transition roadmap for achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. Throughout the year, the Committee continued to review progress on the HKMA's green initiatives, including recommendations to strengthen the HKMA's sustainable procurement policies, procedures, and methodologies. Governance Structure for Sustainability Institutional Sustainability Journey In recognition of the HKMA's dedication to caring for the environment, employees, and society at large, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service (HKCSS) awarded the HKMA the "15+ Years of Caring Together" logo for the 16th consecutive year. The HKMA places significant emphasis on its institutional carbon footprint and has developed internal "Green Office Guidelines" to manage the environmental impact of its operational procedures. Environmental considerations have been integrated into the interior design, operations, and maintenance of its offices. In 2022, BEAM Plus granted Gold certification to certain renovated office areas of the HKMA. This is the second green building certification obtained by the HKMA, following the LEED Gold certification awarded in 2021. Awarded BEAM Plus Interior Building 1.0 Gold Certification The HKMA implements various energy-saving measures. Total energy consumption in 2022 was 4,996.4 MWh (2.8 MWh per person), representing a 24.4% decrease compared to 2015 (Figure 1). Total Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions in 2022 amounted to 2,996.4 tonnes of CO2 equivalent (tCO2e) (1.7 tCO2e per person), a 38.2% reduction compared to 2015 (Figure 2). Figure 1 Figure 2 Greenhouse Gas Emission Intensity (Scopes 1 and 2) The HKMA encourages paperless operations within the institution. Additionally, the HKMA has implemented a print management system requiring staff to log in to printers to confirm each print request, helping to reduce unnecessary printing and toner usage. Where printing is indeed necessary, double-sided printing and black-and-white printing are encouraged. The HKMA is also preparing to implement an internal electronic records retention system. Total paper consumption in 2022 was 20.5 tonnes (0.0114 tonnes per person), a 65.3% reduction compared to 2015 (Figure A). Figure A: Paper Consumption Density The HKMA's waste management continues to adhere to the "4R" principles. In addition to traditional waste, the HKMA also reduces e-waste through technical solutions such as server virtualization and private cloud infrastructure. In 2022, the HKMA engaged an external company for the first time to conduct a waste audit, analyzing the composition of waste generated in the offices. The audit found that food waste accounted for a significant portion of total waste; consequently, the HKMA launched a food waste recycling programme (see "Enhancing Waste Management" on page 41). Total non-hazardous waste generated in 2022 (including general waste and recyclables) was 242.0 tonnes (0.135 tonnes per person), a 4.8% decrease compared to 2015 (Figure 3). Fluctuations in the trend were primarily due to work-from-home arrangements implemented during the peak of the COVID-19 pandemic and the subsequent resumption of office operations after the fifth wave of the pandemic. Figure 3 Non-Hazardous Waste Density The HKMA prioritizes waste reduction at the source and is committed to reducing, reusing, and recycling. In 2022, the HKMA engaged a company for the first time to conduct a waste audit to better understand the composition of waste generated in daily operations (plastics, paper, metals, glass, wood, electronics, etc.) and to provide recommendations for waste reduction. Based on the audit results, the HKMA launched a food waste recycling programme in November, installing food waste collection bins in all pantry areas. Collected food waste is transported daily to an organic resource recycling centre in Hong Kong, where it is converted into renewable energy for power generation. Residues generated during the conversion process can also be made into compost for landscaping and agricultural production. Furthermore, recycling bins are placed at various locations throughout the offices for convenient use. The HKMA shares recycling tips with employees and focuses on further improving source separation of recyclables, as well as providing guidance on handling items such as cardboard boxes, food containers, and beverage bottles. Additionally, we continue to organize activities to raise employees' environmental awareness, explain waste management policies, and encourage the proper use of recycling facilities within the offices. Daily collected food waste is transported to an organic resource recycling centre. Recycling plastic items The HKMA operates two data centres (one operational and one backup). As these account for a major portion of the institution's total energy consumption, the HKMA has adopted green designs and implemented multiple energy-saving measures, including in-row air conditioning systems, LED lighting, and 24-hour monitoring of energy efficiency. Following the completion of a consultant study on the green performance of these data centres in 2022, the HKMA is preparing to implement recommendations to enhance overall energy efficiency. Preparations for obtaining green data centre certification have also commenced. Recognizing the importance of building a sustainability culture, the HKMA regularly launches various programmes and activities to educate and encourage employees to adopt habits conducive to sustainability and to embrace green and digitalized working methods. The HKMA shares green living tips with employees, along with annual statistics on total office energy consumption and paper usage, reminding them to contribute to addressing environmental issues at the individual level; employees are also encouraged to submit suggestions on sustainability matters. Led by a Senior Manager in the Administration Group, a task force gathers employees from different departments to brainstorm ideas and specific measures for promoting a green working environment. Task force members also serve as ambassadors when new green initiatives are launched. The HKMA encourages broader society to adopt more environmentally friendly operating methods and has launched multiple measures to enhance the operational efficiency of the HKMA, the financial industry, and the overall economy, thereby minimizing resource consumption. The HKMA's "System for Electronic Transmission of Returns" (STET) is a one-stop platform enabling banks to submit documents electronically to the HKMA, covering various periodic returns required on a weekly, monthly, quarterly, or annual basis. Another "Electronic Delivery System" (e-Delivery) is a secure electronic communication channel that allows the HKMA to issue notifications and guidelines to banks. Both systems help save significant amounts of paper annually. Regarding the handling of bank complaints and enforcement work, the HKMA has taken measures to support paperless document submission; bank customers can lodge complaints via electronic channels and online forms. The HKMA is also developing a new generation of management information systems to facilitate complaint handling and the transition from paper records to digital records. To reduce paper usage, the Central Money Markets Unit (CMU) has adopted digital signatures in its daily communications with participants, including issuing notifications, account opening and termination letters, and responding to audit confirmations. Looking ahead, the CMU will continue to explore more green measures, including the adoption of automated electronic procedures for internal and external communications. By promoting the use of the Fast and Seamless Payment System "FPS" and stored-value payment instruments, the HKMA encourages the public to adopt electronic payment methods more widely, replacing cash and physical cheques. More information on "FPS" and stored-value payment instruments is available in the chapter "Hong Kong's Status as an International Financial Centre" in the HKMA's 2022 Annual Report. Distributing electronic red packets is simple and convenient, reduces the use of physical red packet envelopes and banknotes, and helps promote sustainability in Hong Kong. To this end, the HKMA continues to actively promote this practice on various social media and traditional platforms, encouraging citizens to distribute electronic red packets via online or mobile banking services using "FPS" or other e-wallet services during the Lunar New Year. Major banks and e-wallet operators also organize various activities to attract users to utilize electronic red packets, such as providing user interfaces filled with Spring Festival atmosphere, enhancing features for greater convenience, and launching lucky draws or cashback promotions. Promotion of electronic red packets on social media For citizens who choose to distribute physical red packets during the Lunar New Year, the HKMA continues to encourage the use of "Welcome Notes"—banknotes that are old in issue but pristine in condition—to be used for red packets. Welcome Notes reduce the need for printing new banknotes, thereby minimizing environmental impact. Feedback from issuing banks indicates that citizens have become increasingly accepting of Welcome Notes in recent years. Coin Collection Scheme This scheme reflects the HKMA's efforts in promoting coin recycling. Coins collected through the scheme are returned to circulation to meet public demand, improving coin circulation efficiency and reducing the need for minting. The scheme operates two coin collection vans, which have served over one million people to date, collecting more than 800 million coins with a total face value of approximately HKD 1.3 billion. In 2022, approximately 78% of users chose to use part or all of their coin value to top up stored-value payment instrument accounts. The HKMA maintains cooperation with the Hong Kong Council of Social Service, deploying coin collection vans to collect coins during the annual charity flag day to support social services. Coin counting machines on the coin collection vans Launched in 2014, the Coin Collection Scheme is the world's first systematic coin collection programme utilizing the mobile van concept. Over the years, it has received numerous local and international awards, with its innovative and environmentally friendly coin handling methods widely recognized. The scheme operates two coin collection vans, each equipped with two high-speed coin counting machines to collect coins exchanged by the public. Citizens can choose to exchange coins for banknotes, use them to top up stored-value payment instrument accounts (such as Octopus cards or e-wallets), or donate them to the Community Chest as charitable funds. In addition to collecting coins, the vans are occasionally deployed for various educational activities, such as student visits.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA) has conducted an independent verification of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's (the "HKMA") Climate Targets (the "Climate Targets"). The Climate Targets were developed in reference to the requirements of the SBTi Corporate Handbook (the "SBTi Corporate Handbook"). The purpose of this verification engagement is to verify whether the Climate Targets were developed in reference to the SBTi Corporate Handbook. This verification engagement was performed in accordance with the "Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information" standards set forth in the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board (IAASB). The verification procedures were designed to express an opinion and draw conclusions to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was conducted in accordance with the requirements of the SBTi Corporate Handbook. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of the data. Our verification work is absolutely independent and impartial. Based on the results of this verification, the HKQAA provides reasonable assurance and concludes that: • The Climate Targets were developed in reference to the SBTi Corporate Handbook.  Shen Xiaoyin, Audit Director, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, March 2023. Verification Statement: The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA) has conducted an independent verification of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's (the "HKMA") 2022 Environmental Data (the "2022 Data"). The 2022 Data includes total energy consumption for 2022, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas (GHG) emission intensity, paper consumption intensity, and non-hazardous waste generation intensity and recycling rate, as well as the changes in these data compared to 2015 levels. The HKMA's GHG emission data were compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (the "GHG Protocol") jointly issued by the World Resources Institute (the "WRI") and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development (the "WBCSD"). The scope of verification covers data for the period from January 1, 2022, to December 31, 2022, as well as relevant data from January 1, 2015, to December 31, 2015, used for year-on-year performance comparison. The verification scope encompasses a total of six office and warehouse assets: four offices located at 1) International Finance Centre Phase II, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) Taikoo Place Phase I, and 4) Kowloon Trade Centre; and two warehouses located at 5) Lothian Industrial Centre and 6) Chong Lee Centre, situated in Kwai Chung and Tsuen Wan, respectively. The purpose of the verification is to provide reasonable assurance regarding the accuracy and reliability of the 2022 Data and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanisms. Within the verification scope, the HKQAA reviewed representative data and supporting evidence selected from the six assets. This verification engagement was performed in accordance with the "Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information" standards set forth in the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board (IAASB). The verification procedures were designed to express an opinion and draw conclusions to obtain a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was conducted in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of data by tracing selected sample data to their sources, and also reviewed and tested the reliability of fundamental procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks. The verification process also included validating the internal data collection and management mechanisms, conducting interviews with representatives responsible for preparing the 2022 Data, and verifying representative data and information. Relevant source data and supporting evidence were also subject to detailed review during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of the data. Our verification work is absolutely independent and impartial. The HKQAA verification team did not participate in the preparation process of the 2022 Data. Based on the results of this verification, the HKQAA provides reasonable assurance regarding the 2022 Data and concludes that: • The 2022 Data are substantially accurate and reliable; • The HKMA's overall data collection mechanism is adequate.  Shen Xiaoyin, Audit Director, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, March 2023.

Expanding and accelerating climate action has become the most urgent priority today. Nearly half of the critical decade for addressing the climate crisis has already passed. To have a chance of limiting global warming to within 1.5 degrees Celsius, global carbon emissions must be reduced by more than 40% over this decade. Yet, greenhouse gas emissions continue to reach record highs. The latest climate science indicates that the window of opportunity to limit global temperature rise to 1.5 degrees Celsius will close soon. The impacts of a 1.1-degree Celsius temperature rise are already clearly felt—extreme weather events, including record-breaking heatwaves and droughts, severe flooding, and storms, are occurring with increasing frequency and intensity worldwide. Hong Kong is no exception. Last September, we experienced a fierce super typhoon, followed closely by a once-in-a-century rainstorm. Despite our robust infrastructure and rapid disaster response capabilities, the impacts were severe, including widespread flooding, traffic disruptions, and damage to multiple roadways. All these serve as a clear reminder that decisive and proactive climate action is urgently needed. Asia faces particularly significant challenges in its low-carbon transition, especially in balancing economic development with sustainability. We require credible transition strategies that appropriately balance climate action with economic growth and social inclusion. This is by no means an easy task. Due to rapid economic development and fast population growth in the region, its carbon emissions account for more than half of global total emissions. At the same time, the high population density in the Asia-Pacific region, combined with its geographical location, makes it particularly vulnerable to rising sea levels and extreme weather. Given the varying stages of economic development across the region, while low-carbon transition may bring new opportunities to some economies, others face enormous challenges in mobilizing the necessary transition financing. Market estimates suggest that the Asia-Pacific region will require over $3 trillion in annual low-carbon transition investment over the next 30 years. As an international financial centre, Hong Kong possesses both the capacity and the responsibility to leverage the power of finance to support low-carbon transition across Asia. As the banking regulator, market facilitator, and responsible investor, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has consistently made significant efforts towards the sustainability agenda. The various chapters of this report will detail the specific measures and initiatives launched by the HKMA over the past year. Additionally, to strengthen the HKMA's internal governance structure and more effectively coordinate sustainability work across different functional areas, we established the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee last year. For detailed information on this committee, please refer to the new chapter on "Governance of Sustainability." Hong Kong banks play a crucial role in supporting Asia's transition to net-zero emissions. Beyond fulfilling our traditional regulatory functions and ensuring that banks properly manage climate risks in our daily supervision, we also act as a facilitator to support the banking sector in providing financing for low-carbon transition. One example is the development of a green taxonomy framework to help banks and other financial institutions identify environmentally sustainable activities, thereby aligning their business decisions with global climate goals. In May, we launched a prototype of the green taxonomy framework for consultation and are now optimizing the framework based on feedback received during the consultation period. Furthermore, as there is growing demand for higher-quality and globally comparable sustainable disclosure information, the HKMA is working with other regulators to develop a clear roadmap for Hong Kong to adopt the disclosure standards issued by the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) in June—a comprehensive global baseline for sustainable reporting. The HKMA's role as a facilitator extends beyond setting frameworks and rules; we are also committed to addressing pain points faced by the industry. Currently, many banks are constrained by data limitations, making it difficult to conduct physical risk assessments. In response, the HKMA will soon launch a cloud-based physical risk assessment platform. Banks can simply input property addresses to assess the impact of physical disasters on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios, thereby assisting banks in managing related climate risks. As a major international financial centre and sustainable finance hub in Asia, Hong Kong has consistently played a bridging role, channeling international investment into sustainable development projects across Asia and supporting the region's low-carbon transition. In recent years, the total value of international green and sustainable bonds issued in Hong Kong has accounted for more than one-third of the Asian market, significantly outpacing other regions. Notably, the governments of Shenzhen and Hainan provinces issued green and sustainable bonds in Hong Kong for the third and second consecutive years respectively in 2023, further affirming Hong Kong's important role as a green gateway connecting mainland China with the rest of the world. The robust development of sustainable bond activities in Hong Kong is partly attributed to the示范 effect of the "Government Green Bond Programme." Since 2019, the HKMA has assisted the government in issuing green bonds worth approximately $25 billion to institutional and retail investors. With each issuance, we have continuously innovated and expanded the features of green bonds, including currency, maturity, and distribution channels, laying the foundation for other public and private green bond issuers in the region. Following the issuance of the world's largest government retail green bond in 2022, we issued the world's first batch of tokenized government green bonds in February 2023. In February 2024, we completed the second batch of tokenized green bond issuances; these bonds are denominated in four major currencies and issued in a digital-native format, marking the world's first multi-currency digital green bonds. At the same time, we have proactively introduced various measures to enhance the vitality and competitiveness of Hong Kong's sustainable finance ecosystem. These efforts span multiple areas, including skills training, data improvement, green fintech, and transition finance. Particularly in talent development, we launched a new "Green and Sustainable Finance" unit under the Banking Professional Qualifications Framework in 2023, providing systematic courses for banking professionals to enhance their understanding and expertise in green and sustainable finance. Transition finance is another key focus area, providing funding for decarbonization activities in high-carbon and hard-to-abate sectors to prevent these industries from failing to transition due to lack of financial support. To support the robust development of transition finance, the HKMA will expand Hong Kong's green taxonomy framework to cover transition activities. We will also broaden the scope of the "Green and Sustainable Finance Fund" to include transition bonds and loans, encouraging regional enterprises to raise transition financing in Hong Kong. Additionally, we will strengthen communication and engagement with relevant stakeholders, leveraging public-private partnerships and blended finance models to attract private sector investment into sustainable development projects that have previously been difficult to finance. Some of the above work requires cross-sectoral collaboration and is primarily coordinated by the Inter-Agency Steering Group on Green and Sustainable Finance, co-chaired by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission. Regional cooperation is equally important. In addition to our long-term collaboration with the International Finance Corporation on the "Green Banking Alliance," the HKMA's Infrastructure Finance Promotion Office joined the "Sustainable Investment Capacity Building Alliance" and the "Green Development Investment and Financing Partnership" in 2023 as founding members. Furthermore, the "Glasgow Net-Zero Asset Owner Alliance" has announced plans to establish a branch in Hong Kong. Through these partnerships, we aim to promote skills training and knowledge sharing, thereby supporting the channeling of capital to sustainable development projects across the region and globally. To foster new business development and knowledge exchange, the HKMA also assisted in organizing the first "Hong Kong Green Week" earlier this year, attracting over 1,600 guests from nearly 30 regions, including top decision-makers in global business and finance, to discuss ways to expand climate financing in the region and forge new partnerships. Chief Executive Eddie Yau delivered a speech at the key event of "Hong Kong Green Week," the "Asia-Pacific Climate Business Forum." As the manager of Hong Kong's official reserves and a significant global asset holder, the HKMA leads by example as a responsible investor. Since 2015, the HKMA has been a pioneer in investing in green and sustainable assets, gradually expanding the Exchange Fund's ESG and green asset portfolio in both public and private markets. In line with the Exchange Fund's "Portfolio" target of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier, the HKMA added an active global equity portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition last year, while also extending the application of a customized low-carbon equity index to another public market asset portfolio. Moreover, the HKMA prioritizes investments in green, social responsibility, and sustainable development bonds, which have outperformed their benchmarks, embodying the principle of "doing well by doing good." In the private market, we continue to pursue green-related investment opportunities and have become anchor investors in two Asia-focused transition investment funds. By the end of 2022, the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund's equity portfolio decreased by 6% and 46% compared to 2021 and 2017 levels respectively, and has consistently remained below the overall market level. As a sustainable institution, the HKMA will continue to strive for progress, developing our sustainability goals and plans based on three pillars: environment, employees, and social responsibility. Specifically, in our journey towards low-carbon transition, the HKMA continuously strengthens our capacity to address climate change by assessing our environmental performance and implementing various internal measures. These measures cover emission reduction, energy efficiency improvement, and waste management, with the ultimate goal of fulfilling our commitment to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. We have formulated plans to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions in the short term and have made good progress towards our mid-term target of reducing Scope 2 emissions by 2030. To attract and retain outstanding talent to fulfill the HKMA's critical functions, in addition to our green goals, we are also committed to promoting the physical and mental well-being of our employees. Furthermore, through collaboration with various stakeholders, we promote financial inclusion, enhance public financial literacy, and raise awareness about preventing financial fraud, contributing to the creation of a caring society. The climate challenge is immense and exceptionally urgent. Economies worldwide are moving towards a more sustainable future, a process that will undoubtedly bring significant changes to financing activities and asset allocation. This transformation carries considerable potential risks but also presents unprecedented opportunities. As a major global sustainable finance hub, Hong Kong has a responsibility to take the lead in addressing these challenges. At the same time, we are well-positioned to seize these opportunities. The HKMA will fully support the industry in providing financing for low-carbon transition; continue to act as a responsible investor and sustainable institution, leading by example, and collaborate with like-minded partners to advance this critically important global agenda. Eddie Yau, Chief Executive

Climate change risks and other sustainability issues are global in nature. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's (HKMA) objective in its sustainability work is to take a leadership role through its policies and operations to ensure that Hong Kong's financial system and the HKMA itself are resilient to climate-related risks, while supporting the transition to a more sustainable economic development path. Through active engagement with international and regional organizations, the HKMA will also contribute to the formulation of green and sustainable finance policies and standards at both regional and global levels. As the banking regulator, the HKMA will further strengthen the banking sector's climate adaptation capabilities and climate risk management. Specifically, key priority areas include: launching a new thematic review of banks' climate risk management practices, accompanied by a new round of consultation meetings as part of assessing progress in implementing regulatory requirements on climate risk management; continuing work to integrate climate factors into the HKMA's supervisory review processes; completing the second round of economy-wide climate risk stress tests, providing guidance to participating banks throughout the process, and sharing observations and lessons learned with the industry; enhancing sustainability disclosures, including collaborating with local authorities to align relevant requirements with the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) Sustainability Disclosure Standards as a global benchmark, and preparing for the implementation of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision's Pillar 3 framework on climate-related financial risks; and sharing guidance on best practices for transition planning with the industry. To promote the healthy development of green and sustainable investment products offered by banks, the HKMA will continue to monitor local and international market and regulatory developments, and maintain close contact with the industry to ensure banks adopt appropriate sales procedures. Additionally, the HKMA will play a facilitator role in driving the development of the green finance ecosystem and supporting banks in financing the economic transition. We will soon publish a local green taxonomy and continue to expand its scope to cover more activities, including transition activities. At the same time, we will continue to explore the application of technology solutions to assist banks in identifying, measuring, and monitoring their climate risk exposures; one example is the upcoming cloud-based platform designed to facilitate banks' physical risk assessments. To enhance professional capabilities, in 2024 we will introduce the "Green and Sustainable Finance" unit at the professional level under the "Banking Professional Qualifications Framework". Hong Kong is well-positioned to serve as a regional and international hub for sustainable finance. To fulfill this role, the HKMA is assisting the government in implementing the proposal in the 2023-24 Budget to expand the scope of the "Government Green Bond Scheme" to include sustainable finance projects, thereby deepening the development of the local green and sustainable bond market. Simultaneously, through the "Green and Sustainable Finance Incentive Scheme", we aim to attract more green financing activities, including transition finance, to Hong Kong. We will also continue to encourage more governments, institutions, and corporations to raise green funds through Hong Kong, and explore potential synergies between green finance and technology. Furthermore, we will continue to support the implementation of the government-funded "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme" to expand Hong Kong's talent pool in green finance. As co-chair of the "Green and Sustainable Finance Inter-agency Steering Committee" (Steering Committee), we will continue to work closely with other agencies to coordinate cross-sectoral policies and initiatives promoting the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. In 2024, the Steering Committee will focus on three key areas: sustainable disclosure, application of technology, and transition finance. As another key priority, through the "Green Banking Alliance", the HKMA and the International Finance Corporation will jointly launch various specialized initiatives in the Asia region, including conducting green finance research, providing unique market analysis, offering targeted professional training for banks, and delivering practical guidance to help financial institutions establish their distinctive green transition pathways. In 2024, we will also strive to deepen our collaboration with the "Glasgow Net-Zero Banking Alliance", the "Investing in Sustainability Capacity Building Alliance", and the "Green Development Investment and Financing Partnership". As a responsible investor, the HKMA commits to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's investment portfolio by 2050 or earlier. We will continue to enhance the sustainability of Exchange Fund investments through a three-pronged responsible investment approach, ensuring the resilience of the asset portfolio throughout the journey toward net zero. Recognizing that achieving the goals of the Paris Agreement requires a comprehensive economic transformation, we are optimizing our net-zero strategy to prioritize assets that deliver positive climate benefits to the real economy, while maintaining the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. As an environmentally conscious institution, the HKMA's carbon reduction strategy will continue to evolve in line with the latest developments in the market, regulation, technology, and other climate-related areas. To further strengthen the HKMA's climate adaptation capacity and risk preparedness, we will explore the feasibility of using technology solutions to assess the impact of physical risks on our office premises. Additionally, we will continue to actively encourage employee participation in our sustainability initiatives, including launching campaigns to foster sustainable habits and optimizing office processes and practices. Moreover, the HKMA will maintain consistent, efficient, and sustainable procurement practices, including evaluating suppliers' ESG practices during contract selection and renewal. Building on the green data centre certification obtained in 2023, the HKMA commits to adhering to the specified certification standards. Regarding regular updates to data centre facilities, in addition to keeping pace with the latest technological advancements, we will integrate green design and operational practices. At the same time, we will continue to reduce electronic waste through the application of technology and convergence, and actively modernize internal systems to improve efficiency and minimize potential risks. Finally, regarding social priorities, the HKMA will identify more community service opportunities for staff, collaborate with the industry to promote financial inclusion and enhance financial literacy, and raise public awareness on preventing financial fraud.

Climate change affects every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating its impacts. Through its multiple roles as a central bank, banking regulator, market facilitator, responsible investor, and sustainability champion, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and across Asia. The HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework that leads the formulation of relevant strategies and policies; oversees the implementation of related measures; and ensures that the HKMA's own operations and working methods integrate sustainability considerations. Committed to sound institutional governance, the HKMA has built a comprehensive sustainability governance framework with clear accountability arrangements and high transparency. This framework ensures that sustainability factors are effectively integrated into the HKMA's strategic planning and decision-making processes, and establishes effective mechanisms to monitor and evaluate the progress and outcomes of sustainability initiatives. The HKMA's sustainability governance framework comprises: the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its relevant sub-committees, which oversee the HKMA's work, including its sustainability efforts, and provide recommendations; the Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, responsible for leading the HKMA's overall environmental, social, and governance (ESG) strategies and policies at the management level; in responsible investing, the ESG Committee under the Investment Office of the Exchange Fund coordinates and oversees ESG-related work within the Investment Office; and for other functional areas, relevant task forces and working groups plan and implement sustainability measures pertaining to banking and market development, as well as the HKMA's own operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Inter-agency Steering Group (Inter-agency Steering Group), jointly established by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), coordinates the efforts of financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders, and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. Given the significant expansion of the scope of the HKMA's sustainability work over recent years, we established the Steering Committee in October as a new central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainability initiatives across the HKMA's different functional areas. Its responsibilities include: providing guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies, and plans for ESG-related matters across the four functional areas of banking, market development, Exchange Fund investment, and internal operations; overseeing the implementation of ESG-related plans by the HKMA's various functional departments; evaluating the HKMA's performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG objectives; and supervising external communication strategies. The Steering Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, with the three Deputy Chief Executives serving as permanent members. Additionally, we invite Assistant Chief Executives responsible for key functions related to green and sustainable development to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on major achievements and future plans for their respective areas. The Steering Committee meets regularly and is supported by relevant working groups under the HKMA's Banking Department, Institutional Development and Operations Department, External Affairs Department, and the Investment Office of the Exchange Fund. In addition to developing and implementing its own sustainability measures, the HKMA jointly established the Inter-agency Steering Group with the SFC in May 2020. As a cross-agency platform, the Inter-agency Steering Group provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sectoral efforts by the financial industry to address climate and environmental risks, thereby reinforcing Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance center in Asia and globally. For details on the work of the Inter-agency Steering Group, please refer to the chapter "Strengthening the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem."

Climate change constitutes a significant risk to the financial system. The HKMA has been committed to strengthening Hong Kong's financial system to build a greener and more sustainable future, contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks face the impacts of various sustainability and climate-related issues in their daily operations. To continue fulfilling their vital role in the financial system and to channel more capital into green and sustainable projects, banks must proactively manage climate risks. As the banking regulator, the HKMA has placed particular emphasis on building banks' capacity to address and manage climate risks, and accelerating their efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economic model. The HKMA is dedicated to formulating various policy measures to enhance the banking system's ability to cope with climate risks. In August, the HKMA issued a Net Zero Transition Planning Notice, outlining high-level principles to assist banks in maintaining safety and soundness during the economic transition to net-zero emissions. Following the issuance of this Notice, we conducted a survey in the fourth quarter with selected banks to understand their transition planning measures. Based on the survey results, we will share observations and best practices regarding transition planning with the industry, and will organize seminars or workshops to facilitate the exchange of experiences. Regarding disclosure requirements, in response to recent international developments, including the International Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB) published in June and the consultation launched in November by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (Basel Committee) on the Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks, the HKMA is strengthening its efforts to improve the sustainability-related disclosure framework for Hong Kong banks. Specifically, the HKMA is collaborating with local relevant authorities and stakeholders to develop a comprehensive roadmap for Hong Kong that aligns with the ISSB. During the year, the HKMA enhanced its supervision of banks' climate risk management and provided recommendations to help banks further improve their climate resilience and climate risk management capabilities. The HKMA has made significant progress in implementing its two-year plan to incorporate climate risk factors into the banking regulatory framework. Climate risk management has now been established as a standing agenda item in prudential supervisory meetings with bank management. Banking supervisors have also adopted the enhanced CAMEL rating system1, which incorporates climate risk factors, to assess banks' risk profiles and risk management systems. As part of the implementation of the two-year plan to incorporate climate risk factors into the banking regulatory framework, the HKMA revised the "Green" Assessment Framework to focus on banks' transition planning measures.
