The HKMA is also reviewing the Supervisory Review and Evaluation Process (SREP) used to assess and monitor banks' capital adequacy and determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, to encourage banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks in addressing climate risks. Key work priorities under the two-year plan in 2023: Following the completion of the 12-month implementation period for complying with Supervisory Policy Manual (SPM) Module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management", the HKMA launched a thematic review on climate-related risk governance in the second quarter. This thematic review covered four key areas: governance structures for climate-related risks, oversight of climate strategies, oversight of climate-related risk management, and organizational culture, awareness, and communication. The HKMA made several improvements to its climate risk stress testing framework, including the introduction of a new five-year scenario to assess the potential impact on banks of simultaneous economic and climate change shocks. Following these improvements, and as part of the HKMA's regular regulator-led stress testing program, the second round of climate risk stress testing commenced in June to conduct a comprehensive assessment of banks' climate risk exposures and further enhance their climate risk management capabilities. A total of 44 banks participated in this stress test, representing an increase of over 60% compared to the first pilot program in 2021. The HKMA also hosted a Climate Risk Stress Testing Forum in November, attended by up to 300 banking professionals. By facilitating the sharing of experiences among banks, this event helped deepen the industry's overall understanding of climate risk measurement. The HKMA also conducted a series of consultation meetings to review banks' progress in implementing SPM Module GS-1 "Climate Risk Management". The HKMA held meetings with bank management to discuss their work on climate risk management and common challenges faced by the industry, and reviewed information provided by banks and other public information to assess their relevant progress. The HKMA provided targeted recommendations to banks, encouraging and supporting them to continue strengthening their climate risk management capabilities in line with the HKMA's regulatory expectations. Amid growing global attention to climate change and efforts to address it, the HKMA has noted an increasing demand for green and sustainable investment products, with some banks offering relevant products to meet client needs. In light of this, the HKMA completed a thematic review on banks' sale of green and sustainable investment products and issued a Notice in November outlining the standards the HKMA expects banks to achieve and sharing observed good practices. This Notice covers multiple areas, including product due diligence, disclosure, governance and controls, staff training, and book building, aiming to mitigate potential greenwashing risks and enhance investor confidence, thereby promoting the sound development of such investment activities. The HKMA will continue to monitor the latest trends and market developments. The HKMA is committed to promoting the application of technology in green and sustainable banking. For example, technology can improve data availability and risk analysis, enhancing banks' ability to manage climate risks. The HKMA is about to launch a beta version of a cloud-based platform for banks to assess the impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings under different climate scenarios. Furthermore, the HKMA continues to collaborate with other central banks and regulators to explore how technological solutions can assist in physical risk assessment. On the other hand, the HKMA also encourages the adoption of sustainable anti-money laundering (AML) practices through the application of advanced analytics and artificial intelligence, reducing the consumption of compliance-related resources. In 2023, the HKMA launched an online shared data submission platform, fully automating the financial crime risk data collection process, thereby strengthening banks' operational workflows for submitting AML-related data in a sustainable manner. In September, the HKMA organized the "Green Fintech Competition" to seek market-ready solutions to help the banking industry address challenges in the following areas: (i) net-zero transition or transition planning; (ii) climate risk management; (iii) green and sustainable finance; and (iv) sustainability or climate-related disclosure and reporting. The competition attracted a total of over 85 entries from approximately 70 companies. In December, the HKMA held the "Green and Sustainable Banking Seminar," providing a platform for the banking and technology sectors to explore the role of low-carbon technologies and green fintech in the net-zero transition in Hong Kong and Mainland China, and announced the results of the "Green Fintech Competition." The event attracted approximately 400 participants from banks, technology companies, regulators, and academia. To enhance transparency across financial markets and ensure greater consistency in green and sustainable finance decision-making, the HKMA, with the assistance of advisory firms, developed a local green taxonomy framework. In May, the HKMA published a discussion paper on the "Prototype of the Hong Kong Green Taxonomy Framework" to solicit stakeholder views on the establishment and implementation of a green taxonomy. Based on the consultation results, the HKMA is fine-tuning the framework prototype and identifying other areas for the next phase of framework development. The HKMA participates in the work of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF); the FATF has recognized environmental crimes as predicate offenses for money laundering, and in light of the linkages between AML and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) issues, this area is attracting increasing attention from regulators. The HKMA is acutely aware that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system and has therefore incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into financial risk analysis and research to strengthen its current monitoring efforts. In the process of continuously monitoring financial stability risks, the HKMA takes climate change into account and includes analysis of climate-related risks in its various Financial Stability Reports. Through active participation in the Scenario Design and Analysis Working Group under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA has helped further enrich climate scenarios, enabling central banks and regulators to better understand the impact of climate change on the macroeconomy and finance. As a member of the Transition Planning Working Group under the Financial Stability Board (FSB), the HKMA participates in analyzing the interactions between transition planning of financial and non-financial companies and financial stability, enabling policymakers to adopt a forward-looking and dynamic perspective on climate-related financial risks. In terms of research, the HKMA has conducted multiple applied research projects exploring the impact of climate change and broader ESG issues on the financial sector and the economy. Research topics include climate risk exposures of the banking sector and investment funds2, ESG capital flows3, the impact of climate change on property prices4, and the ripple effects of corporate ESG performance in global supply chains5. The results of these studies have enhanced the HKMA's understanding of the impact of climate change and ESG issues on financial stability, aiding in the formulation of relevant policies. Locally, these studies help strengthen the HKMA's continuous monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate risks on financial stability. Externally, the HKMA also shares research findings with a wide range of stakeholders through international activities on climate-related matters and various channels such as the HKMA Research Memoranda. The HKMA's "Liquidity Arrangement Framework" is a collateralized standby liquidity facility providing timely liquidity support to banks in need. The HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations into the assessment of eligible collateral under this framework in accordance with NGFS recommendations. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risks and promoting sustainable finance as a mainstream practice. Through such participation, the HKMA helps facilitate policy dialogue at the international and regional levels on addressing climate change and its impact on financial stability, and draws insights to help strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong's financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as the region's leading green and sustainable finance hub, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) is committed to enhancing market awareness and engagement, providing the necessary infrastructure and enablers, and supporting international initiatives to align with global standards. Throughout the year, the HKMA worked closely with local and international partners to build a more robust ecosystem, driving the further development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. The Cross-sector Steering Committee on Green and Sustainable Finance (the Steering Committee), co-chaired by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), is responsible for coordinating the financial sector's response to climate and environmental risks, accelerating the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong, and supporting the Government's climate strategies. Since its establishment, the Steering Committee has made significant progress. In January 2024, the Steering Committee announced key measures to support Hong Kong in seizing sustainable finance opportunities, with major areas of work including sustainable disclosure, ecosystem building, transition finance, and green fintech. Specifically, a Sustainable Disclosure Working Group was established to develop a roadmap for Hong Kong's adoption of the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards. This roadmap will cover four key areas: sustainability reporting, assurance, data and technology, and skills training. Additionally, a Transition Finance Working Group was set up to explore methods to support financial institutions and enterprises in transition planning and reporting. The Steering Committee has also strengthened the sustainable finance ecosystem through cross-sector skills training and data enhancement. Particularly in the area of data, we continue to promote the adoption of the Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire for Non-listed Companies, launched in 2022 by the Steering Committee in collaboration with CDP. The Steering Committee will continue to keep pace with the latest developments in the green and sustainable finance sector and enhance Hong Kong's status as a regional and global hub for green and sustainable finance. In January 2024, the Steering Committee announced three new key initiatives to capture investment and financing opportunities arising from the low-carbon transition in the Asia-Pacific region. To support industry skills training, the Green and Sustainable Finance Centre under the Steering Committee implemented the Government's "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme," providing subsidies to practitioners, students, and graduates undertaking relevant training and obtaining related qualifications. As of December 2023, a total of 46 international and local training programmes or qualifications were registered as eligible under the scheme, and over 560 subsidy applications were approved. The HKMA has also launched a foundational-level module on "Green and Sustainable Finance" under the "Banking Professional Qualifications Framework." This module aims to foster talent development in the banking sector and enhance the overall professional competence of practitioners. In 2024, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with the banking industry to develop the professional-level module of this unit to meet the rapidly growing demand for green and sustainable finance professionals in the sector. To help financial institutions and enterprises, especially SMEs, better understand key climate and sustainability-related issues—including climate risk management, sustainability reporting, greenhouse gas emissions calculation, and transition planning—the HKMA, in collaboration with relevant Government bureaux and departments, as well as global partners such as CDP, the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ), and the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF), organized a series of seminars and thematic workshops throughout the year, attracting participants from the financial services and corporate sectors. Regarding students, following the launch of the "Sustainable Finance Internship Programme" in 2022, training sessions were held in January and February 2023, enabling interns and university bachelor's degree graduates to deepen their understanding of sustainable finance. Recognizing the potential of technology in bridging climate-related data gaps and improving data quality, the HKMA is committed to making such data more accessible and enhancing its quality to support informed decision-making and effective climate action. In February 2024, the Steering Committee launched a series of website optimization measures to provide a one-stop source of green and sustainable finance information for financial institutions, enterprises, and the public. Key optimization items include an electronic platform for sustainable disclosure, greenhouse gas emissions calculation and estimation tools, and more centralized, user-friendly, and searchable data and resources. During "Hong Kong Green Week," the Steering Committee, in collaboration with Cyberport and the Investment Promotion Authority, co-organized the event "Leveraging Technology to Catalyse Sustainable Finance," showcasing leading green innovation solutions and Hong Kong's strengths in green technology. "Hong Kong Green Week – Finance Theme" was held from February 26 to March 1, 2024, during which various sustainability-themed events attracted over 1,600 guests from nearly 30 regions, including representatives from financial institutions, enterprises, central banks, international organizations, government bodies, academia, and consulting firms. The flagship event of "Hong Kong Green Week" was the "Asia-Pacific Climate Business Forum," co-organized by the HKMA and the International Finance Corporation (IFC). The forum gathered over 400 guests, including top decision-makers in global business and finance, to discuss solutions for unlocking climate finance in the Asia-Pacific region. This two-day event covered a wide range of topics, including energy transition, decarbonization of heavy industry, the circular economy, the future of sustainable finance, and emerging climate technologies in Asia-Pacific's emerging and developing markets. The forum received strong support from both public and private sectors, co-hosting over 10 roundtables, seminars, and other exchange activities. Topics covered included climate finance, carbon markets, electric vehicle supply chains, net-zero transition financing, green finance taxonomies, and green development financing in the Belt and Road region. Additionally, the HKMA and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) co-organized the "Asia Climate Finance Roundtable" on February 29, 2024, to discuss key measures to scale up climate finance and the role of central banks and regulators in climate risk management. These activities form part of the HKMA's broader efforts to promote and enrich Hong Kong's green and sustainable finance ecosystem, serving as valuable platforms for participants to drive new business development, share knowledge, and explore new opportunities to address climate finance challenges in the Asia-Pacific region. The HKMA has also been actively supporting the development of green and sustainable finance in the region. In November 2020, the IFC and the HKMA launched the "Green Banking Alliance," a collaborative platform bringing together regional financial institutions, banking industry associations, research institutions, and technology innovators to jointly develop green commercial banking. Since March 2021, the Alliance has held 22 training events and roundtables, attracting over 7,300 participants from across the Asia-Pacific, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Americas. In October, the Alliance, in collaboration with Crédit Agricole CIB, published its second Frontier Issues Report titled "Developing Ambitious Climate Strategies for Green Banking: Case Studies." In October, the Alliance and Crédit Agricole CIB jointly released the Frontier Issues Report titled "Developing Ambitious Climate Strategies for Green Banking: Case Studies." During the year, the HKMA's Infrastructure Financing Promotion Office joined the newly established "Capacity Building Alliance for Sustainable Investment" (CASI) and the "Green Investment and Financing Partnership" (GIFP) initiated by the "Belt and Road" Green Development International Alliance. Collaboration with CASI and GIFP will facilitate capacity building and knowledge sharing, and channel more capital towards green and sustainable projects in Asia and beyond. In August 2023, GFANZ announced the establishment of its Hong Kong chapter to support net-zero efforts by local and Mainland Chinese financial institutions. The HKMA is assisting GFANZ in an advisory capacity. To demonstrate the Government's commitment to addressing climate change, promoting green finance, and developing Hong Kong into a more sustainable and livable city, the Government launched the "Government Green Bond Programme" in 2018. The HKMA has assisted in the issuance of green bonds under the programme. To date, the Government has issued approximately USD 25 billion worth of green institutional and retail bonds, with proceeds allocated to over 70 green government projects, such as green buildings, waste management and resource recovery, energy efficiency, and energy conservation. To enhance the transparency and accountability of the programme, the Government publishes an annual "Green Bond Report," detailing the allocation of proceeds from green bond issuances and their expected environmental benefits. In the 2023-24 financial year, the Government continued its regular issuance of green institutional bonds, issuing approximately USD 6 billion worth of green bonds in June. This tri-currency issuance covered bonds in USD, EUR, and RMB with various tenors, attracting diverse categories of investors. The subscription response was strong, with total subscription amounts nearing USD 30 billion. The RMB bond issuance increased from RMB 10 billion in January to RMB 15 billion, and a 10-year RMB bond was introduced for the first time, helping to extend the Government's RMB yield curve and further enrich offshore RMB product options. The strong response from global investors to the Government's green bond issuances reflects their recognition of Hong Kong's commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. In October, the Government issued the second tranche of green retail bonds totaling HKD 20 billion, further promoting market development and advancing financial inclusion. This issuance provided citizens with a stable-return investment opportunity, enabling them to both participate in and benefit from Hong Kong's green finance development.

As a major global asset owner and manager, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) plays a pivotal role in advancing green and sustainable finance to support the global climate agenda. The HKMA has long been a pioneer in responsible investment. Since 2015, it has led the way in investing in green and sustainable assets, requiring its external investment managers to actively exercise asset ownership and integrate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors into the investment management of the Exchange Fund. Guided by the principle of "preserving capital first, achieving long-term growth," the HKMA invests prudently, believing that a comprehensive focus on ESG factors helps mitigate investment risks while unlocking long-term sustainable value. As one of the first central banks to sign the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI) and to set a "Net Zero by 2050" target for its portfolio, the HKMA is committed to advancing its responsible investment journey, emphasizing sustainability, particularly the urgent issue of climate change, with the aim of enhancing the resilience of the Exchange Fund and pursuing superior risk-adjusted long-term returns. As a responsible investor, the HKMA contributes to building a robust green and sustainable financial ecosystem, collaborating with like-minded investors, regulators, and international organizations to establish industry standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment across the financial sector and among central banks. Through oversight and collaborative measures, the HKMA strives to foster a future where finance and sustainable development go hand in hand.Diagram 1: The Responsible Investment Journey of the Exchange FundComprehensive and reliable ESG information is crucial for integrating sustainability and planning credible climate transitions to achieve net zero targets. In fulfilling its commitments to the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) Glasgow Declaration and the cross-agency supervisory strategy plan for green and sustainable finance, the HKMA has taken concrete action by preparing this chapter on the responsible investment of the Exchange Fund in accordance with the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD). The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, establishes the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office (EFIO) in the investment management of the Exchange Fund. The primary guiding principle sets the tone for the HKMA to practice responsible investment while safeguarding the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. The Investment Committee, a sub-committee of the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, oversees ESG and climate-related risks associated with Exchange Fund investment projects. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management policies and monitors their implementation through regular reports from the Sustainable Investment Team of the EFIO. As shown in Diagram 2, the ESG Committee under the EFIO, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, is responsible for coordinating and overseeing all ESG-related work within the EFIO. Motions and progress discussed at the ESG Committee's quarterly meetings are reported to the Chief Executive of the EFIO. Additionally, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and attended by the Chief Executive of the EFIO and the Chief Strategy Officer, meets biannually to provide guidance on ESG policies and measures across different functions of the HKMA, including the EFIO, to realize the HKMA's overall ESG objectives.Diagram 2: Governance Structure for Responsible Investment at the Exchange Fund Investment OfficeAs illustrated in Diagram 1, the EFIO embarked on its responsible investment journey in 2016, initially focusing on managing ESG risks that could impact the financial performance of the Exchange Fund. As sustainability rapidly evolved, transcending risk considerations to become a key strategic priority for major institutions worldwide, the EFIO re-examined its approach to responsible investment. July 2023 marked another milestone with the establishment of a new Business Strategy Department at the EFIO, led by the Chief Strategy Officer, responsible for coordinating and leading the strategic development of the EFIO. This department incorporated the former Responsible Investment Task Force, which was previously under the Risk Management and Surveillance Division, now renamed the Sustainable Investment Team. This strategic realignment reflects the HKMA's shift in focus for responsible investment from a risk-based approach to a more proactive and forward-looking stance in addressing sustainability-related investment matters. The Sustainable Investment Team works closely with various teams within the EFIO to integrate ESG factors and assists senior management in managing ESG, particularly climate-related, risks and opportunities across different investment projects:Public Market Investments: The Credit, Regulatory and Surveillance Committee, composed of senior personnel from the EFIO, reviews the integration of ESG factors into credit risk models based on inputs from the Sustainable Investment Team and monitors the ESG status of the fixed income portfolio through regular reports from the Risk Management and Surveillance Division. Furthermore, the Sustainable Investment Team participates from an ESG perspective in the selection, appointment, and monitoring processes of external investment managers for the equity portfolio (see the section "Promoting Active Exercise of Asset Ownership" under "Risk Management" on page 40).Private Market Investments: The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers ESG-related assessments made by the private market investment and risk management teams for each investment proposal.The HKMA recognizes that the physical and transition risks, as well as related opportunities, posed by climate change will affect the long-term performance and value of Exchange Fund investment projects. The United Nations Environment Programme's "2023 Emissions Gap Report" projects that unless greenhouse gas emissions are further reduced globally, the global average temperature will rise by 2.5 to 2.9 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels by 2030. The urgent need for more ambitious policies, technological development, or behavioral changes to control temperature rises may exacerbate transition risks such as asset devaluation or stranding. At the same time, increasingly frequent and severe extreme weather events pose additional physical risks to investment projects. The HKMA believes that investing in a greener future aligns with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund; therefore, it places particular emphasis on climate-related factors when integrating ESG considerations. In 2022, the HKMA set a target for the Exchange Fund portfolio to achieve net zero emissions by 2050 or earlier, further demonstrating its commitment to the global climate agenda. The HKMA continues to strengthen its three-pronged approach, with a clear focus on decarbonization and transition. The following sections will detail these approaches.Diagram 3: The HKMA's Three-Pronged Approach to Responsible InvestmentIn the journey towards net zero, the HKMA tends to engage proactively rather than excluding or divesting from investable projects. First, maintaining a diversified and robust asset portfolio is critical to achieving the primary investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe, potentially impacting investment returns and risks. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA can seize opportunities to invest in companies undergoing transition that possess excellent technology and sound corporate governance to address evolving global climate trends, including those in high-emission industries. Second, addressing climate change requires the transformation of core "brown" industries. Merely excluding related investments or divesting does not help solve carbon emission problems. Instead, the HKMA supports these industries by deploying strategic capital and actively exercising asset ownership, encouraging them to adopt sustainable and low-carbon operational practices, thereby driving beneficial changes for themselves and the world. In response to market developments, the HKMA is refining its net zero investment strategy to pursue transition outcomes that align with both the Exchange Fund and global net zero targets through a comprehensive approach, while adhering to its guiding principles for responsible investment. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continues to seek sustainable investments and opportunities to promote climate transition and enhance the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund portfolio (Diagram 4).The HKMA's responsible investment maintained strong momentum in 2023. In public markets, the HKMA launched a new active global equity portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition, managed by an external investment manager, and expanded the application of customized low-carbon equity indices to another asset portfolio managed by an external investment manager. Additionally, the performance of green, social, and sustainable bonds prioritized by the HKMA outperformed their benchmarks, demonstrating the concept of "doing well by doing good." In private markets, the HKMA actively built a resilient long-term growth portfolio, seizing investment opportunities expected to benefit from long-term economic development trends such as climate and energy transitions. For example, during the year, the HKMA invested in two transition investment funds primarily focused on Asia, reflecting its commitment to addressing Asia's climate transition needs.Diagram 4: Continued Implementation of Measures to Promote ESG InvestmentThe HKMA has invested in a company specializing in producing eco-friendly thermoplastic materials from unsorted household waste (including organic matter such as food waste) and non-recyclable materials. Unlike traditional chemical recycling systems that rely on high-energy, high-temperature environments to produce plastics, this company has pioneered a low-temperature production method powered entirely by solar arrays. These plastic materials, produced 100% from waste, can serve as a sustainable and versatile alternative to oil-based resins commonly used in industries such as retail and durable consumer goods. Moreover, these materials are compatible with existing standard manufacturing processes and advanced technologies such as 3D printing. The company firmly supports the circular economy. The diagram below illustrates the positive environmental outcomes generated by its advanced plastic production process:Managed by the International Finance Corporation (IFC), MCPP is an innovative initiative that combines funds from institutional investors with the IFC's own capital to scale up sustainable financing for private companies in emerging markets. The HKMA committed two tranches of USD 1 billion each to MCPP in 2017 and 2019, and further collaborated with the IFC to create a new global climate-related investment platform, "MCPP One Planet," in 2021. This platform is the world's first cross-sector emerging market loan portfolio aligned with the Paris Agreement. Through the MCPP program, the HKMA has committed to providing loans for 80 sustainable development projects across 19 sectors, including infrastructure, agriculture, real estate, and manufacturing, in 38 developing countries. The IFC has collected data on MCPP loans. According to the IFC's report, the HKMA's loan commitments support emerging markets and developing countries in areas such as economic transformation and human resource development. Specifically, projects funded by the HKMA are expected to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by approximately 5.6 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent annually, equivalent to the emissions from a typical gasoline car traveling 14 billion miles.Diagram 5: Predicted Average Annual Benefits of the HKMA's Loan Commitments to MCPP Since 2020The green and sustainable financial ecosystem is the cornerstone of future global sustainable development. The HKMA actively collaborates with like-minded investors and partners to promote responsible investment and enhance industry capabilities.

The HKMA is committed to becoming a sustainable organization, employing a multi-pronged approach to reduce its carbon footprint, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. Beyond promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA also prioritizes employee well-being and social responsibility, while striving to advance financial inclusion and enhance public financial literacy. As a responsible institution, the HKMA has set sustainability goals under three pillars: environment, employees, and social responsibility. The Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (the Steering Committee), established in October and chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, serves as the primary decision-making body for all organizational sustainability measures. Preceded by the Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainable Development Committee, the Steering Committee leads the HKMA in formulating the vision, strategies, and policies for organizational sustainability and social responsibility matters. At the departmental level, the Assistant Chief Executive (Institutional Development and Operations) oversees the implementation of sustainability activities and regularly submits progress reports to the Steering Committee. The Green Office Task Force and the Volunteer Service Group provide support for coordinating organizational sustainability efforts; the former serves as a platform for brainstorming on creating a green working environment, while the latter aims to foster a culture of participation in volunteer activities. The HKMA has developed a roadmap to guide its transformation journey. Key focus areas include implementing carbon reduction strategies in daily operations, such as operating green buildings and data centers, practicing green mobility, adopting energy-saving measures, digital tools, and more environmentally friendly working models, reducing waste, and building a sustainability culture. The HKMA also plans to utilize embodied carbon tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions, while adopting carbon offset measures for emissions that are difficult to reduce. In addition to the aforementioned environmental commitments regarding its daily operations, the HKMA continues to introduce more environmentally friendly operating schemes for the wider society, covering channels for banks to submit electronic documents and communications, as well as electronic payment and coin collection schemes for the general public. To strengthen and maintain its operational capacity, the HKMA employs a professional workforce, builds a talent pool, and prioritizes employee well-being. In terms of social responsibility, the HKMA encourages employees to participate in volunteer and charitable activities; considers selecting social enterprises in procurement; promotes consumer education in financial services; and collaborates with the banking sector to ensure equitable access to basic banking services for all sectors of society. The remainder of this chapter details the aforementioned strategies. Under the HKMA's overall corporate risk management framework, the Risk Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers the potential risks and threats the HKMA faces in its daily operations, including those arising from climate change. The physical impacts of climate change, such as flooding or other damage caused by increased extreme weather events, could affect the HKMA's offices and hinder employee commuting. To manage physical risks, the HKMA regularly updates its Business Continuity Plan to respond to extreme weather situations. The HKMA also regularly conducts evacuation and backup facility activation drills to ensure employees are always prepared to implement business continuity measures. The design of the offices also incorporates various measures to mitigate potential risks. Transition risks may affect the HKMA's energy consumption, air travel, and waste management. The HKMA has been monitoring the transition risks it faces by tracking its own greenhouse gas emissions, waste generation, as well as energy and paper consumption. The HKMA's climate goal is to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions across Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 (air travel) in all areas of organizational operations by 2050 or earlier. As a near-term emission reduction target, the HKMA plans to completely eliminate Scope 1 emissions by converting all its existing vehicles to electric vehicles; and with 2015 as the baseline year, reduce Scope 2 emission intensity by 63% by 2030 or earlier through various carbon reduction and offset strategies. Despite challenges in determining Scope 3 emissions, the HKMA will adopt a multi-pronged approach to the extent practicable to minimize greenhouse gas emissions from Scope 3 (e.g., paper consumption, waste generation, and air travel). The HKMA's long-term and near-term emission reduction targets were formulated with reference to the "Science Based Targets initiative" methodology, which has also been verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA). The HKMA has appointed the HKQAA to verify the emissions, energy consumption, paper usage, and waste data disclosed in this report. The scope and criteria for verification are set out in the "Verification Statement" section of this report. In 2023, in addition to publishing the "Annual Report 2022", the HKMA also issued its "Sustainability Report 2022" independently for the first time. The HKMA's enhanced ESG reporting efforts have been recognized, winning the ESG Award in the "Public Sector Category" at the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants' "Best Corporate Governance and ESG Awards 2023". The HKMA is the first financial regulatory authority to receive an award in this category. The adjudication panel commended the HKMA for achieving high ESG standards, noted that the "Sustainability Report" is clear and easy to read, and highlighted that appointing an independent body to verify its target-setting methodology and the environmental data disclosed in the report reflects its commitment to high transparency and accountable reporting. Furthermore, the HKMA received the highest rating, the Gold Award, in the "Non-profit and Charitable Organizations" category at the Hong Kong Management Association's "2023 Best Annual Report Awards". The adjudication panel praised the HKMA's annual report for clearly presenting comprehensive financial information and effectively utilizing infographics, demonstrating the HKMA's determination to enhance financial literacy and promote financial inclusion. In recognition of the HKMA's dedication to caring for the environment, employees, and society as a whole, the Hong Kong Federation of Social Service has awarded the HKMA the "15+ Years of Caring Together" logo for 17 consecutive years since 2006. The HKMA is committed to properly managing the environmental impacts of its operations. Its internal "Green Office Guidelines" provide employees with guidance on resource utilization and the generation of office waste. The HKMA has integrated environmental factors into the design, operation, and maintenance of its owned and leased offices. During office renovations, existing furniture and decoration materials are reused as much as possible to reduce waste, and environmentally friendly construction and decoration materials are prioritized. The HKMA has consistently followed this practice, and consequently, in 2021 and 2022, it received Gold-level certifications under LEED and the "BEAM Plus Interior Building Assessment" for the renovated office sections completed at the International Finance Centre Phase 2. Adopting new technologies and making optimal use of existing technologies to improve energy efficiency remains one of the HKMA's key focus areas. In addition to promoting good habits, such as turning off unnecessary lighting within work areas outside of office hours to save electricity, other energy-saving measures include using LED lighting equipment, motion sensors, setting air conditioning temperatures at appropriate levels, and optimizing energy use in IT network infrastructure. The HKMA's energy consumption has continued to decrease, reaching 2.59 MWh per person in 2023, a 29.7% reduction compared to the 2015 baseline (Figure 1). Given the nature of the HKMA's daily operations, its greenhouse gas emissions primarily stem from electricity generated from fossil fuels. In 2023, the combined intensity of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions from purchased fuels and electricity was 1.48 tCO2e per person, a 45.2% reduction compared to 2015 (Figure 2). In addition to standardizing equipment, office software, and conference facilities, the HKMA has adopted digital tools and technologies, automated and streamlined workflows, and built a digitalized working environment to enhance online collaboration within the organization. Paperless meetings have become the primary mode of meeting at the HKMA. To further reduce paper consumption and improve efficiency, various internal administrative affairs are primarily handled through electronic processes. Furthermore, the HKMA encourages employees to integrate green and digital working models, replacing paper documents and communications with digital alternatives. Meanwhile, the implementation of an electronic record-keeping system is also underway. The aforementioned green and digital measures have yielded positive results. The HKMA's paper consumption intensity in 2023 was 11.55 kg per person, a significant 64.8% reduction compared to 2015 (Figure 3). Since the post-pandemic period, most international activities have returned to physical formats, and to promote the development of Hong Kong's status as an international financial centre, it is unavoidable that relevant HKMA employees need to travel overseas for official duties. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages employees to take direct flights or combine different official trips whenever feasible when participating in overseas activities. At the organizational level, the HKMA reduced its Scope 3 emissions by 126 tCO2e in 2023 through the purchase of Sustainable Aviation Fuel. Additionally, the HKMA participated in the "Gold Standard" certified carbon offset program to offset remaining carbon emissions from air travel; this program implements waste-to-energy, solar power generation, and provides efficient and cleaner cooking facilities in developing countries. The HKMA will continue to make similar arrangements in 2024. The HKMA's procurement process considers sustainability and environmental factors. As part of a comprehensive review of the organization's procurement policies and procedures, the current practice of procuring green products has been formalized and complies with the environmental specifications of the government's "Environmental Procurement List," particularly in the procurement of electrical appliances and office consumables. Furthermore, ESG factors and innovative proposals that help enhance productivity and efficiency have been incorporated into the tender evaluation criteria. At the same time, all suppliers must commit to complying with environmental regulations. Adhering to the "4R" principles—Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle—the HKMA adopts a three-pronged approach to minimize waste generation and manage waste disposal. Additionally, the HKMA conducted two waste audits in 2022 and 2023 to assist in formulating targeted waste management strategies. Details of the non-hazardous waste generated, including general waste sent to landfills and various types of recyclable waste, are included in the "Performance Summary" section on page 56. In 2023, the HKMA participated directly for the first time in the red packet recycling program organized by the building management company of the International Finance Centre office tower. Employees submitted approximately 3,000 used but still pristine red packets. These red packets were subsequently handed over to an environmental organization for distribution to the public for use during the following Lunar New Year. Given that the HKMA's operations and backup data centers constitute the major portion of the organization's total energy consumption, both data centers have been upgraded to meet the highest standards set by BEAM Plus for existing data centers, achieving optimal Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE). In 2023, the HKMA's two data centers received "Gold" and "Platinum" ratings respectively under the "BEAM Plus Existing Data Centres" assessment guidelines issued in 2021; the HKMA is the first and only organization in Hong Kong to receive such ratings. Enhancing the energy efficiency of the two data centers has always been a key focus of the Technical Team. To this end, the team adopted green design principles in renovation projects and implemented energy-efficient best practices to lower PUE and achieve relevant targets, including 24/7 monitoring of the data centers' environmental facilities and continuous improvement of environmental factors such as air circulation and temperature settings. As the Technical Team continuously improves energy utilization in the data centers, the HKMA commissioned external consultants in December 2021 to conduct a review to comprehensively assess the green level of the data centers and formulate recommendations for further enhancing performance in various aspects. The study was completed in mid-2022. Shortly after the completion of the study, the HKMA began preparing to qualify for the "Green Data Centre" certification under the BEAM Plus certification scheme. The certification process is very comprehensive and rigorous. Throughout 2023, the Technical Team implemented optimization measures based on the consultants' recommendations to enhance energy performance as well as health elements within the data center working environment.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA) has independently verified the 2023 environmental data ("2023 Data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority ("HKMA"). The 2023 Data includes total energy consumption for 2023, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, GHG emissions from business air travel, paper consumption, and non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfills and recyclable waste), along with their respective intensities and changes compared to 2015 levels. Additionally, the 2023 Data includes the quantity of food waste generated during the year, its intensity, and the change compared to the baseline when the HKMA launched its food waste recycling programme in November 2022. The HKMA's GHG emissions data have been compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (GHG Protocol) jointly developed by the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The scope of verification covers data for the period from 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2023, as well as relevant data from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2015 used for annual performance comparison (excluding food waste quantities). The verification scope encompasses a total of five office and warehouse assets: four offices located at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) Taikoo Place Phase I, 4) Kowloon Trade Centre, and one warehouse at 5) Lark Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification is to provide reasonable assurance regarding the accuracy and reliability of the 2023 Data and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanisms. Within the verification scope, the HKQAA reviewed representative data and supporting evidence selected from the five assets. This verification was conducted in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), "Assurance Engagements Other Than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information," issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were specifically designed to form an opinion and conclusions to achieve a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was determined in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. It tested the completeness and accuracy of data by tracing selected sample data back to their sources, and reviewed and reliability-tested the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks. The verification process also included validating internal data collection and management mechanisms, interviewing representatives responsible for preparing the 2023 Data, and verifying representative data and information. Relevant source data and supporting evidence were also carefully reviewed during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for data collection and reporting. Our verification work was absolutely independent and impartial. The HKQAA verification team did not participate in the preparation of the 2023 Data. Based on the results of this verification, the HKQAA provides reasonable assurance on the 2023 Data and concludes that: the 2023 Data are substantially accurate and reliable; and the HKMA's overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Shen Siu-yin, Review Manager, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, April 2024.

The threats posed by climate change are imminent, making it imperative to accelerate global climate action. The World Meteorological Organization has confirmed 2024 as the warmest year on record and the first in which global temperatures exceeded the critical threshold of 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Meanwhile, although global greenhouse gas emissions saw a slight moderation during the pandemic, they have recently reached new highs, underscoring the inadequacy of current climate mitigation measures. As we address global warming, climate-related risks are poised to intensify, with unpredictable impacts on the economy and financial markets. Furthermore, the current tense geopolitical landscape, the increasing fragmentation of the global economic order, heightened concerns over energy security, and an uncertain economic outlook all present greater challenges for nations in tackling climate change. The transition to a low-carbon economy requires substantial and sustained financial support. Globally, Asia faces the most severe transition challenges. As noted by the World Economic Forum, Asia is not only the engine of global economic growth but also the region most vulnerable to climate change impacts. Therefore, Asia plays a pivotal role in determining whether the world can successfully achieve its net-zero emission goals. As Asia's leading international financial center, Hong Kong must strengthen its leadership role and fully leverage the power of finance to support and drive the regional transition. To this end, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) unveiled its "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" last year, outlining our vision and roadmap for progressively integrating sustainability into the core of the financial system. Our work focuses on two fronts: enhancing the financial sector's capacity to manage climate-related risks and assisting the industry in seizing new opportunities. Simultaneously, we lead by example. The HKMA's sustainability efforts encompass four key areas: supporting the banking sector's journey to net zero, investing in a sustainable future, promoting net-zero financing, and driving more inclusive sustainable development. The banking system plays a critical role in Hong Kong's and Asia's net-zero transition, yet it faces significant risks in this process. In the "Action Plan," we have set ambitious targets, requiring all banks to strive for net-zero emissions from their own operations by 2030 and net-zero financed emissions by 2050. We also require all banks to enhance their disclosure of climate-related risks and opportunities. While continuously strengthening banks' climate risk management, we provide guidance for their transition planning to help them improve their transition capabilities and better manage associated risks. We are also engaging with relevant stakeholders to advance preparations for aligning Hong Kong's sustainable disclosure requirements with international standards, aiming to further enhance industry transparency in related activities. Additionally, we are optimizing the Hong Kong Sustainable Finance Taxonomy launched last May by incorporating more sustainable activities, including transition activities. We aim to guide more capital toward sustainable and transition-related projects by providing clear criteria. Climate change brings significant physical and transition risks that could affect the long-term financial performance and value of Exchange Fund investment portfolios. However, it also presents opportunities for growth and positive impact. Our experience demonstrates that investment returns and positive sustainable impacts can be aligned without conflict. In light of this, we are committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's "portfolio" by 2050 and have pledged in the "Action Plan" to support Asia's climate transition through Exchange Fund investments. Currently, sustainable investments already account for over 10% of the "portfolio." To further promote sustainable investment in the region, the HKMA established strategic partnerships last November with the Asian Development Bank, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, and the International Finance Corporation to accelerate the region's low-carbon economic transition through co-investment. Furthermore, in September last year, we issued our first "HKMA ESG Expectations" document to further encourage fund managers to actively exercise asset ownership and adopt sound sustainable investment practices. Capital mobilization is particularly crucial for accelerating the regional transition. As an international financial hub and the preferred venue for arranging international sustainable bond issuances for Asian issuers (including provincial and municipal governments in mainland China), Hong Kong plays a vital role in guiding capital to speed up the regional transition. The "Action Plan" outlines the vision of developing Hong Kong into the region's preferred platform for sustainable finance financing and the goal of promoting sustainable finance innovation. From leveraging the demonstration effect of the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme" to drive green bond innovation (including the issuance of the world's first multi-currency digital bonds in February last year), to expanding the scope of the "Green and Sustainable Finance Co-financing Scheme" to include transition financing tools in May last year, and to launching the "Digital Bond Co-financing Scheme" in November last year, we have consistently encouraged regional issuers to utilize Hong Kong's financial platforms to raise funds for decarbonization and transition. Achieving a robust transition requires not only capital and innovation but also an inclusive and accessible sustainable development ecosystem. This includes reliable sustainable development data, high-transparency information disclosure, and industry professionals equipped with relevant knowledge and skills. Accordingly, in the "Action Plan," we have committed to supporting the promotion of high-quality and comprehensive sustainable disclosure and to addressing the gaps in sustainable finance talent and knowledge in the region. We have made significant progress in assisting relevant stakeholders and facilitating sustainable disclosure, particularly by providing user-friendly climate disclosure templates to promote sustainable disclosure among small and medium-sized enterprises. We also launched a professional-level unit on "Green and Sustainable Finance" under the Banking Professional Qualification Framework last November to enhance the relevant knowledge and skills of local banking practitioners. Additionally, through the inaugural Hong Kong Green Week held in February last year and other events, we have engaged various sectors in discussions on sustainable development to foster collaboration and innovation. Internally at the HKMA, we are committed to ensuring our operations align with our sustainability vision. We pledged in the "Action Plan" to achieve net-zero emissions from our own operations by 2030, accelerating our original commitment by 20 years. Furthermore, we are actively preparing to meet international sustainable disclosure standards in accordance with the roadmap issued by the government. We began adopting electric vehicles in 2024 and have incorporated low-carbon emissions as a screening factor in our procurement processes. Simultaneously, we continue to enhance efficiency through digitalization, foster a culture of sustainability within the organization, and motivate staff to actively participate in sustainability initiatives. Multilateral cooperation has always been the cornerstone of global climate action, but the reshaping of the international landscape and drastic geopolitical shifts have introduced uncertainties. However, climate change is an undeniable fact and is progressively intensifying. In our efforts to address climate change, the current situation does not allow for any slackening of resolve. We firmly believe that advancing an orderly and inclusive transition will help mitigate the impact of climate risks on Hong Kong's financial system while creating opportunities in the process. As we enter 2025, we will continue to forge ahead, striving to advance sustainability work and deepen relationships with like-minded partners. Despite facing severe challenges, we remain dedicated to supporting the construction of a sustainable future for Hong Kong, Asia, and beyond.

Climate change is a major challenge facing the current generation. As an international financial centre and a sustainable finance hub in Asia, Hong Kong is committed to playing a pioneering role in supporting sustainable development across Asia and globally. In October 2024, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) unveiled its "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" (the "Action Plan"), outlining its vision in this area, including future directions, timelines for achieving various objectives, and expectations for industry collaboration in advancing related initiatives. The HKMA plans to strengthen the climate risk resilience of Hong Kong's financial sector and its own capabilities by formulating strategic policies, enhancing regulatory engagement, and improving internal operations, while also driving the region's transition towards a more sustainable economy. Through active participation in international and regional discussions, the HKMA is also committed to exerting influence in shaping green and sustainable finance policies and standards at both regional and global levels. As the banking regulator, the HKMA focuses on enhancing the climate resilience of the banking sector and supporting banks in maintaining safety and soundness during their transition to net-zero emissions. Our key priorities for 2025 include: - Launching a new round of thematic reviews on banks' climate risk management practices and conducting the third round of consultation meetings to assess banks' implementation of relevant HKMA regulatory requirements and further strengthen their climate risk management capabilities; - Finalising the integration of climate risk stress testing into the HKMA's supervisory stress testing framework; - Continuing to advance the incorporation of climate factors into the HKMA's supervisory review processes; - Preparing to formulate relevant regulatory requirements for the implementation of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision's forthcoming Pillar 3 disclosure framework on climate-related financial risks and the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) standards in the local banking sector; - Completing the development of new Unit GS-2 of the "Supervisory Policy Manual" to provide guidance to banks on transition planning; and - Sharing good practices on climate risk management and the application of green fintech with the industry. Beyond its role as the banking regulator, the HKMA also acts as a facilitator, committed to promoting the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem and supporting banks in financing the transition. We have launched Phase I of the "Hong Kong Sustainable Finance Taxonomy," providing the industry with a tool to identify green and sustainable economic activities and facilitating related financing. The HKMA has commenced work on Phase II of the Taxonomy to expand its scope, including the inclusion of transition elements, additional green economic activities, and climate adaptation objectives. Furthermore, building on the success of the third FiNETech event in 2024 and the Green Fintech Competition in 2023, we will host another green fintech event in 2025 to encourage banks to adopt green fintech solutions. Hong Kong is well-positioned to support sustainable financing needs in the region. To reinforce this role, we will continue to assist the Government in implementing the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme," whose expanded scope will now include sustainable projects such as social responsibility initiatives. This will help deepen the development of the local green and sustainable bond market and serve as a demonstration for other potential issuers in the region. In addition, we will continue to provide funding through the "Green and Sustainable Finance Incentive Scheme" to encourage more borrowers in the region to use Hong Kong's financing platforms to raise sustainable capital. We will also enhance our promotional efforts to encourage more governments, institutions, and enterprises from mainland China and other regions to raise green funds in Hong Kong. At the same time, we will continue to catalyse and support sustainable finance innovation, including providing funding through the "Digital Bond Incentive Scheme" to prospective issuers of digital green bonds. Although market demand for high-quality sustainable disclosures from institutions and enterprises is growing, entities vary in their capabilities and preparedness to make such disclosures, and some may require additional guidance and support. In response, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with other members of the Inter-agency Steering Group on Green and Sustainable Finance to make sustainable disclosure more accessible and inclusive. For instance, we will continue to provide banks and their clients with richer climate disclosure-related tools, including user-friendly sustainable disclosure templates and supporting utilities; explore how technology can make existing resources more convenient and accessible; and partner with major local industry organisations to deliver training needed by the sector. The sustainable finance market is rapidly evolving, necessitating the expansion of the local talent pool and the bridging of knowledge gaps in Hong Kong and the region. The HKMA's key initiatives in 2025 include collaborating with the banking sector to develop professional-level training courses under the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module of the "Banking Professional Qualifications Framework," and identifying areas where further training is needed through the forthcoming "Future Banking Talent 2026–2030" study. In addition, we plan to work with key stakeholders to enhance the promotion of the Government-funded "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme" and review its scope of applicability. At the regional level, the HKMA will continue to collaborate with the International Finance Corporation through the "Green Bankers' Alliance" to launch targeted initiatives in Asia, including conducting green finance research, providing unique market analysis, offering targeted skills enhancement and training support, fostering community engagement, facilitating potential green investment opportunities, and providing practical guidance to assist banks in developing roadmaps to integrate green finance as a core business. As a responsible investor, the HKMA is committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's investment portfolio by 2050 or earlier to support the broader economic transition. We will continuously enhance the sustainability of Exchange Fund investments through a pragmatic and rigorous responsible investment approach, primarily focusing on the long-term resilience of the asset portfolio while exploring investment opportunities that can deliver positive climate outcomes. The HKMA is committed to setting an example in institutional sustainability. In line with the accelerated net-zero commitment timeline announced in the "Action Plan," the HKMA will progressively integrate environmental and social factors into its strategies, risk assessments, and reporting through pragmatic steps, continuing to drive institutional sustainability. Specifically, in 2025, we will conduct a double materiality assessment to deepen our understanding of the potential financial and non-financial impacts of climate change and other sustainability issues, ensuring our focus remains on material matters. Additionally, we will carry out an energy audit and utilise technology solutions to assess the significant impacts of climate risks on our offices and operations, thereby enhancing our climate resilience and risk preparedness. We support the Government's "Hong Kong Sustainable Disclosure Roadmap" and are actively preparing to make disclosures in accordance with the ISSB standards. In 2025, the HKMA will continue to uphold its commitment to selecting data centres for planned upgrade projects in accordance with energy efficiency and energy-saving principles. We will also expand digital initiatives to promote sustainability and improve efficiency, including developing digital tools and platforms to support paperless processes and waste reduction, and enhancing the overall digital experience for our staff, banks, and the public.

Climate change impacts every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating these effects. Through its multiple roles as a central bank, banking regulator, market facilitator, responsible investor, and sustainability champion, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) contributes to promoting and accelerating the transition to net-zero emissions in Hong Kong and across the Asia region. The HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework that leads the formulation of relevant strategies and policies, oversees the implementation of related measures, and ensures that the Authority's own operations and practices integrate sustainability considerations. In its commitment to sound corporate governance, the HKMA has put in place a comprehensive sustainability governance framework featuring clear accountability arrangements and high transparency. This framework ensures that sustainability factors are effectively integrated into the HKMA's strategic planning and decision-making processes, and establishes effective mechanisms to monitor and evaluate the progress and effectiveness of sustainability initiatives. The HKMA's sustainability governance framework includes: - the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee and its relevant sub-committees, which oversee the HKMA's work, including its sustainability efforts, and provide recommendations; - the Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (the Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, which leads the Authority's overall environmental, social, and governance (ESG) strategies and policies at the management level; - in the area of responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office coordinates and supervises ESG-related work within the Office; and - in other functional areas, relevant task forces and working groups are responsible for planning and implementing sustainability measures related to banking and market development, as well as the HKMA's internal operations. At the cross-sectoral level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Sectoral Steering Group (the Cross-Sectoral Group), jointly established by the HKMA and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), coordinates the efforts of financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders, and other stakeholders to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. Given the significant expansion of the scope of the HKMA's sustainability work over recent years, we established the Steering Committee in October 2023 as a central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainability initiatives across the HKMA's different functional areas. The Steering Committee: - provides guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies, and plans related to ESG matters across four functional areas: banking, the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, Exchange Fund investments, and internal operations; - oversees the implementation of ESG-related plans by the HKMA's various functional departments; - evaluates the HKMA's performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG objectives; and - supervises external communication strategies. The Steering Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, with three Deputy Chief Executives serving as permanent members. In addition, we invite Executive Directors responsible for key functions related to green and sustainable development to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on major achievements and future plans of their respective areas. The Steering Committee meets regularly and is supported by relevant working groups within the HKMA's Banking Department, Corporate Development and Operations Department, External Relations Department, and the Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition to formulating and implementing its own sustainability measures, the HKMA jointly established the Cross-Sectoral Group with the SFC in May 2020. As a cross-institutional platform, the Cross-Sectoral Group provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sectoral efforts by the financial sector to address climate and environmental risks, thereby reinforcing Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance centre in Asia and globally. For details on the work of the Cross-Sectoral Group, please refer to the chapter "Strengthening the Green and Sustainable Finance Ecosystem."

Climate change can pose risks to the financial system. The HKMA has been committed to enhancing the resilience of Hong Kong's financial system to climate risks, while contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks are exposed to various sustainability and climate-related issues in their daily operations and must proactively manage climate risks. At the same time, as key players in the financial system, banks play a crucial role in directing capital towards green and sustainable projects. As the banking regulator, the HKMA has placed particular emphasis on building banks' capacity to respond to and manage climate risks, and accelerating their efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economic model. In October, the HKMA launched the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" (the "Action Plan"), outlining the HKMA's vision to further consolidate Hong Kong's position as a regional sustainable finance hub and support sustainable development in Asia and globally. The Action Plan comprises eight targets across four areas. To assist the industry in achieving the relevant policy objectives for banks, we have been carrying out the following initiatives: All banks are committed to achieving net-zero emissions from their own operations by 2030 or earlier, and net-zero emissions from their financed portfolios by 2050 or earlier. All banks are enhancing transparency on climate-related risks and opportunities. In December, the HKMA shared good practices on transition planning with the industry and launched a consultation on the draft of Unit GS-2 "Transition Planning" of the Supervisory Policy Manual. The new unit aims to provide guidance on enhancing banks' capacity to respond to the net-zero transition and manage associated risks. In addition, we are reviewing the supervisory review process used to assess and monitor banks' capital adequacy and determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements. The objective is to incorporate factors proposed by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (the Basel Committee) for effectively managing climate-related financial risks into the assessment process, and to encourage banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks (including transition planning) in addressing climate risks. The HKMA has been committed to aligning local sustainable disclosure requirements with international standards, including the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) Standards and the Basel Committee's Pillar 3 disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks. Specifically, the HKMA is analyzing the latest developments in sustainable disclosure and supporting the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants in conducting a technical feasibility study on the adoption of the ISSB Standards. Promoting green and transition finance is key to implementing the Action Plan. In May, the HKMA published the Hong Kong Sustainable Finance Taxonomy (the "Taxonomy") to address industry concerns regarding greenwashing and to help direct capital flows towards green and sustainable activities. The Taxonomy covers 12 economic activities across four sectors, aiming to align with the Common Ground Taxonomy as well as the taxonomies of mainland China and the European Union, while incorporating relevant local elements. We have commenced the second phase of work to expand the scope of the Taxonomy and are consulting widely with stakeholders to further facilitate the mobilization of green and sustainable capital. During the year, the HKMA further strengthened its supervision of banks' climate risk management and committed to supporting banks in building their capacity to manage climate-related risks and opportunities and respond to climate change. The HKMA also completed all work under its two-year plan formulated in 2022 to integrate climate risks into banking supervisory processes. To promote banks' enhanced capacity in managing climate risks, the HKMA shared good practices observed in thematic reviews and consultation meetings with the banking industry, mainly including: - Establishing a robust governance framework that clearly defines the responsibilities of the board of directors and senior management; - Ensuring effective oversight of key areas of climate-related risk matters: (1) promoting and monitoring the effective formulation and implementation of climate strategies; (2) exercising appropriate oversight over climate-related risk management; and (3) fostering a strong climate risk culture within the institution. In August, the HKMA organized a Balanced Supervision Roundtable on climate risk management. At the roundtable, bank representatives and HKMA participants exchanged views on various climate risk-related topics, including challenges banks face in climate risk management, climate risk stress testing, transition planning, and finance. The roundtable provided an interactive platform for information sharing and assisted the HKMA in its work on climate risk supervision and other related areas. The HKMA launched a thematic review of banks' climate risk management frameworks and practices, assessing their robustness and adequacy against the supervisory expectations set out in Unit GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" of the Supervisory Policy Manual. The thematic review covered the entire risk management process, including risk identification, measurement, monitoring, reporting, control and mitigation, as well as climate risk scenario analysis and stress testing. The HKMA held the second series of consultation meetings to assess the progress of a new batch of banks in implementing Unit GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" of the Supervisory Policy Manual and to understand the challenges they face. The consultation meetings also covered the latest regulatory and market developments in climate-related areas, including transition planning, disclosure frameworks and standards, and greenwashing issues. We provided feedback and guidance tailored to individual banks' circumstances to support their climate risk management efforts. In 2024, the HKMA completed the second round of the Banking Sector Climate Risk Stress Test (CRST), involving 21 retail banks and 25 Hong Kong branches of international banking groups. The results showed that under various scenarios (including assumptions of simultaneous climate risks and macroeconomic downturns), Hong Kong's banking sector continued to demonstrate strong resilience against severe climate-related shocks. Compared with the CRST pilot, participating banks significantly enhanced their capabilities in measuring and assessing climate risks. A report detailing the CRST results and good practices observed by the HKMA during the process was published in February 2025. Recognizing the numerous challenges banks face regarding data and methodologies in climate risk management, the HKMA has been committed to various initiatives to promote the application of technology to address these challenges. To address the lack of physical risk-related data and analytical tools for climate risk assessment, the HKMA launched a Physical Risk Assessment Platform in May, enabling banks to evaluate the potential impact of physical risks on residential and commercial buildings in Hong Kong under different climate scenarios. Looking ahead, the HKMA will enhance the platform by incorporating user feedback and adding more local data. In addition, the HKMA is collaborating with relevant stakeholders to promote the adoption of green fintech solutions by banks and the broader financial services industry. During the year, we released a Practical Guide on Application and two RegTech Use Case Briefs (in English), outlining technological solutions for Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) and sustainability assessment, as well as greenwashing risk management. We also hosted the third "FiNETech" event, bringing together over 150 financial institutions and technology companies to explore cooperation in green fintech. The HKMA is well aware that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system and has therefore incorporated a broader range of climate factors and scenarios into financial risk analysis and research to strengthen current monitoring efforts. In its ongoing monitoring of financial stability risks, the HKMA takes climate change into account and includes analysis of climate-related risks in various financial stability reports. Through active participation in the Scenario Design and Analysis Working Group under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA has helped further enrich climate scenarios, assisting central banks and regulators in understanding the impacts of climate change on the macroeconomy and finance. In November, the NGFS published the fifth version of its Long-term Climate Macro-Financial Scenarios, providing a reference for forward-looking climate risk assessment.
