As a member of the Transition Planning Working Group under the Financial Stability Board, the HKMA participated in analyzing the interaction between transition planning of financial and non-financial corporations and financial stability, enabling policymakers to view climate-related financial risks from a forward-looking and dynamic perspective. The HKMA published the "Practical Guide on Banks' Application of Green Technology" (in English), providing best practices for financial institutions to leverage green technology and promote their net-zero transition. In terms of research, the HKMA has conducted multiple applied research projects exploring the impacts of climate change on the financial sector and the overall economy. Research topics include the cross-border transmission of climate transition risks, the role of corporate environmental performance in withstanding monetary policy shocks, the impact of climate-related factors on foreign direct investment flows, and the role of the financial sector in the transition to a low-carbon economy. The above research outcomes not only deepen our understanding of how climate change affects financial stability but also provide valuable insights into the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, aiding policy formulation. Locally, these studies help strengthen the HKMA's ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impacts of climate change on financial stability. Research results are also shared with a wide range of stakeholders through international forums and various channels, including the HKMA Research Memoranda. The Hong Kong Monetary and Financial Research Centre (the Centre), responsible for research under the Hong Kong Institute for Finance, published a research paper on the impact of carbon pricing on corporate performance. The study provides evidence that low-emission enterprises can derive significant benefits from carbon pricing and highlights its role in improving efficiency by reallocating resources from high-emission to low-emission enterprises. The study was published in the Centre's "Insights from Monetary Research" and shared with local and international scholars and policy researchers. The HKMA's "Liquidity Arrangement Framework" is a collateralized standby liquidity facility that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations into the assessment of eligible collateral under this framework. The HKMA actively participates in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risks and mainstreaming sustainable finance. Through such participation, we help facilitate policy dialogue internationally and regionally on addressing climate change and its impacts on financial stability, and draw lessons to strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong's financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as the region's leading hub for green and sustainable finance, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) is committed to enhancing market awareness and engagement, providing necessary infrastructure and drivers, and supporting relevant international initiatives to align with global standards. As outlined in the HKMA's "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" (the "Action Plan"), the Authority is dedicated to enhancing the green and sustainable finance ecosystem by promoting net-zero financing and fostering more inclusive sustainable development. Specifically, we are committed to positioning Hong Kong as the preferred sustainable financing platform for borrowers in the region and globally, supporting technological innovation in the green sector of financial markets, improving sustainable disclosure within the industry, expanding the local pool of green talent, and addressing knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in Hong Kong and the region. Positioning Hong Kong as the region's and global preferred sustainable financing platform catalyzes sustainable finance innovation, supports high-quality and comprehensive sustainable disclosure, and fills regional gaps in sustainable finance talent and knowledge.To demonstrate the Government's determination to address climate change, promote green finance, and develop Hong Kong into a more sustainable and livable city, the "Government Green Bond Programme" was launched in 2018. To date, the HKMA has assisted the Government in issuing green bonds equivalent to approximately USD 28 billion to institutional and retail investors. The proceeds have been allocated to over 110 government green projects, including green buildings, waste management and recycling, energy efficiency, and energy conservation. We seize every issuance opportunity to continuously innovate and expand the features of green bonds, including currency, tenor, and distribution channels, laying the foundation for other public and private green bond issuers in the region. In 2024, to enhance the Programme's impact and further consolidate Hong Kong's status as a green and sustainable finance hub, the scope was expanded to include sustainable projects, and it was renamed the "Government Sustainable Bond Programme" (the "Sustainable Bond Programme"). To improve the transparency and accountability of the Sustainable Bond Programme, the Government publishes an annual "Green Bond Report," detailing the allocation of proceeds from green bond issuances and their expected environmental benefits. In July, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing institutional green bonds equivalent to approximately USD 3 billion under the Sustainable Bond Programme. This tri-currency issuance covered bonds in Renminbi (RMB), US dollars, and euros with varying tenors. These bonds attracted participation from various investor categories, generating a strong subscription response with total subscriptions exceeding USD 15 billion. Notably, the 20-year and 30-year RMB green bonds marked the Government's first issuance of such instruments and represent the longest-dated RMB bonds issued by the Government to date, providing a new benchmark for the market and further demonstrating the exemplary role of the Sustainable Bond Programme. These bonds also further enriched the range of offshore RMB investment products available in Hong Kong. Furthermore, the enthusiastic response from global investors to the Government's green bonds reflects their endorsement of Hong Kong's commitment to promoting green and sustainable development.To encourage more regional borrowers to utilize Hong Kong's financing platform to raise sustainable development funds, the HKMA continues to implement the "Green and Sustainable Finance Funding Scheme," launched in May 2021, which provides funding for eligible green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong. Widely welcomed by the industry, the Scheme has, as of the end of 2024, granted funding for approximately 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong with a total value exceeding USD 140 billion. The Scheme was extended by three years to 2027 in May 2024, with its scope expanded to cover transition bonds and loans. The purpose of this extension and expansion is to encourage borrowers in relevant industries across the region to utilize Hong Kong's transition financing platform to gradually reduce carbon emissions.- Granted funding for approximately 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong with a total value exceeding USD 140 billion (as of the end of 2024).- Extended by three years to 2027 and expanded to cover transition financing instruments.Meanwhile, the HKMA has actively promoted Hong Kong's sustainable financing platform, achieving desirable results. For instance, in August, the People's Government of Shenzhen issued its fourth offshore local government bond in Hong Kong, totaling RMB 7 billion, comprising RMB 2.7 billion in green bonds, RMB 1 billion in sustainable bonds, and RMB 0.9 billion in social responsibility bonds. In September, the People's Government of Guangdong Province issued its first offshore bond in Hong Kong, totaling RMB 5 billion, including RMB 1.5 billion in green bonds. In October, the People's Government of Hainan Province also issued its third offshore bond in Hong Kong, totaling RMB 3 billion, including RMB 1 billion in blue bonds and RMB 1 billion in sustainable bonds. These issuance activities repeatedly highlight Hong Kong's unique role in facilitating the flow of green and sustainable funds between Mainland China and the rest of the world. Through these measures, Hong Kong has consolidated its position as the preferred platform for sustainable financing in Asia. According to statistics published by the International Capital Market Association (ICMA), in 2024, Hong Kong continued to be the largest hub in Asia for arranging international green and sustainable bond issuances, with a total value of USD 43.1 billion, accounting for 45% of the regional total.To catalyze sustainable finance innovation, the HKMA assisted the Government in issuing two landmark batches of tokenized green bonds in 2023 and 2024: the world's first tokenized sovereign green bonds and the world's first multi-currency digital bonds. These issuances demonstrate the Government's support for market participants in the region in applying asset digitization and innovative technologies in the fields of green and sustainable finance. Additionally, in November, the HKMA launched the "Digital Bond Funding Scheme" to promote the issuance of digital bonds in Hong Kong, including digital green bonds, thereby encouraging and supporting the innovative development of the local green and sustainable finance market.The Working Group on Sustainable Disclosure under the Cross-Sector Steering Group on Green and Sustainable Finance (the "Steering Group") has been working on the adoption of the "International Financial Reporting Standards on Sustainability Disclosures" (ISSB Standards) in Hong Kong. In December 2024, the Government released the "Hong Kong Sustainable Disclosure Roadmap," providing a clear path for large public interest entities to fully adopt the ISSB Standards no later than 2028. The HKMA has been closely collaborating with local and international partners to support entities at different stages of preparation in achieving high-quality sustainable disclosure, making such disclosure more accessible and inclusive. Notably, we continue to encourage the application of the "Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire for Non-Listed Companies" (the "Questionnaire"), launched in 2022 by the Steering Group in collaboration with CDP. This Questionnaire provides an easy-to-use disclosure template, facilitating sustainable disclosure for companies, including small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). An electronic version of the Questionnaire was launched in February 2024 to facilitate online submission by companies (see the QR code below). The HKMA is optimizing the Questionnaire based on industry feedback and the latest international developments to make it more user-friendly, with specific measures including identifying core questions within the Questionnaire and providing common usage scenarios. Furthermore, we are striving to enhance the compatibility of the Questionnaire with other supporting tools on the Steering Group's website. For more information on the Questionnaire, please refer to the relevant webpage.The HKMA leads by example, making high-quality sustainable disclosures in its "Sustainability Report" in accordance with the latest global standards to demonstrate its commitment. The report contains rich content regarding the HKMA's institution-specific climate-related operational risks, as well as plans and progress in achieving climate goals. For details on our own operational sustainable disclosures, please refer to the chapter "A Sustainable HKMA."Given the rapidly changing nature of the sustainable finance market, to address knowledge and talent gaps, the HKMA is strengthening skills training in the banking sector and promoting knowledge sharing with other regulators and international stakeholders. To enhance the knowledge and skills of local banking professionals in sustainable finance, the HKMA, together with the Hong Kong Institute of Bankers (HKIB), launched the foundational level of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the "Banking Professional Qualifications Framework" in July 2023. This module aims to assist banking professionals in acquiring knowledge and developing relevant professional capabilities in green and sustainable finance more effectively, covering four main areas of work: (1) Green and Sustainable Finance Products and Services; (2) Sustainable/Climate Risk Management; (3) Sustainable Disclosure and Reporting; and (4) Sustainable Strategy, Compliance, and Governance. Additionally, the professional level of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module, targeted at mid-to-senior level banking professionals responsible for related work, was launched in November. To provide necessary training for banking professionals, the HKIB, as the administering body for the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module, launched the foundational level training course in May. Following the launch of the professional level in November, the HKMA will collaborate with the banking industry in 2025 to develop professional-level training courses. To understand further skills and training needs in the banking sector, the HKMA is currently collaborating with the industry on the "Future Banking Talent 2026-2030" study, with results targeted for publication in 2025. This joint study follows the "Future Banking Talent 2021-2025" document published in June 2020. The findings of this follow-up study will provide important references for the industry to formulate and adjust talent training strategies and measures, supporting the sustainable development of the banking sector.The HKMA also continues to assist in the implementation of the Government-funded "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme" through its collaboration with the Steering Group, funding training for practitioners, graduates, and students in sustainable finance. As of December 2024, 85 international and local courses have been registered as eligible training courses under the Scheme, and over 5,700 reimbursement applications have been approved. The Government announced in the "2025-26 Budget" that the Scheme will be extended to 2028. The HKMA is committed to leveraging its experience to promote skills training and knowledge sharing through regional and international cooperation. As a founding member of the "Coalition for Sustainable Investment Capacity Building" (CASI), the HKMA's Infrastructure Financing Facilitation Office co-organized a two-day training workshop with CASI in Hong Kong in June, discussing global sustainable finance markets, policy frameworks, and innovative tools. Furthermore, the HKMA supports the establishment of a branch of the "Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero" (GFANZ) in Hong Kong in October and will leverage GFANZ's network and expertise to strengthen skills training in transition planning and transition finance.

As a significant global asset owner and manager, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) actively leads the development of green and sustainable finance. Leveraging its experience in demonstrating that financial performance and positive impact can be mutually reinforcing, the HKMA adheres to the principles of responsible investment in managing the Exchange Fund, prioritizes sustainable assets, and requires its external investment managers to exercise active ownership. Guided by the principle of "capital preservation first, long-term value creation," the HKMA invests prudently, believing that due attention to Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) factors helps mitigate investment risks while unlocking long-term sustainable value. As a committed signatory to the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI), the HKMA is dedicated to advancing its responsible investment agenda. We place particular emphasis on sustainability, especially the urgent challenge of climate change, aiming to enhance the resilience of the Exchange Fund and achieve superior risk-adjusted long-term returns. We integrate ESG factors in a pragmatic and orderly manner, continuously exploring various investment instruments to channel capital into sustainable investments across different asset classes (Figure 1). By leveraging its role as a major investor, the HKMA contributes to the development of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem. In September, the HKMA published the "HKMA ESG Expectations" and made the document available to investment partners through its annual ESG workshop and website. We collaborate with like-minded investors, regulators, and international organizations to establish industry standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment within the financial sector and among central banks. Through these collaborative efforts, we are committed to fostering a future where finance and sustainable development go hand in hand. In October, the HKMA unveiled the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" (the "Action Plan"), outlining its commitment to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund "portfolio" by 2050 or earlier, and mobilizing partners to support the transition to a low-carbon economy, further solidifying its pledge to invest in a sustainable future. The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, establishes the responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Exchange Fund Investment Office (EFIO) in the management of the Exchange Fund's investments. The primary guiding principle sets the tone for the HKMA to practice responsible investment while safeguarding the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. The Investment Committee, a sub-committee of the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for overseeing ESG and climate-related risks associated with Exchange Fund investment projects. The Investment Committee reviews the responsible investment framework and risk management policies and monitors implementation through regular reports from the Sustainable Investment Team within the EFIO. As shown in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the EFIO, chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer, is responsible for coordinating and overseeing various ESG initiatives within the EFIO. Motions and progress discussed in the ESG Committee's quarterly meetings are reported to the Chief Executive Officer of the EFIO. Additionally, the Green and Sustainable Steering Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA and attended by the CEO and Chief Strategy Officer of the EFIO, meets regularly to provide guidance on ESG policies and measures across different HKMA functions, including the EFIO, to achieve the HKMA's overall ESG objectives. The Sustainable Investment Team works closely with various teams within the EFIO to integrate ESG factors and assists senior EFIO personnel in managing ESG, particularly climate-related, risks and opportunities across various investment projects:- Public Market Investments: The Credit, Regulation, and Oversight Committee, comprised of senior EFIO personnel, reviews the integration of ESG factors into credit risk models, incorporating input from the Sustainable Investment Team. It monitors the ESG status of the fixed-income portfolio through regular reports from the Risk Management and Oversight Department. Furthermore, the Sustainable Investment Team participates in the selection, appointment, and monitoring processes of external investment managers for the equity portfolio from an ESG perspective (for details, see the section "Promoting Active Ownership" under "Risk Management" on page 39).- Private Market Investments: The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers ESG-related assessments made by the private market investment and risk management teams for each investment proposal.The HKMA recognizes that the physical and transition risks, as well as related opportunities, posed by climate change can affect the long-term financial performance of Exchange Fund investment projects. The United Nations Environment Programme's "2024 Emissions Gap Report" projects that unless there is a rapid, large-scale global mobilization to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, the global average temperature will rise by 2.6 to 3.1 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Uncertainties regarding policy changes, technological advancements, and behavioral shifts in response to rising temperatures may exacerbate transition risks, leading to increased market volatility and affecting asset valuations. Meanwhile, the increasing frequency and severity of extreme weather events also bring additional risks of physical damage and financial losses to investment projects. Amid these challenges, the shift by governments and industries toward sustainable solutions has created potentially attractive long-term investment opportunities in low-carbon solutions, emerging technologies, and sustainable infrastructure. The HKMA believes that investing in a sustainable future aligns with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund, hence placing particular emphasis on climate-related factors in integrating ESG considerations. The HKMA has set a target for the Exchange Fund "portfolio" to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier and continues to advance this goal through an orderly, three-pronged approach (see Figure 3). In 2024, the HKMA published the "Action Plan," which consolidated the Exchange Fund's commitments and efforts related to climate transition (see Figure 4). To support the transition to a low-carbon economy, the HKMA tends to engage proactively rather than exclude or divest from investable projects.Investing in a Sustainable Future: Achieving Net-Zero Emissions for the Exchange Fund "Portfolio" by 2050 or Earlier- Actively expanding the scope and variety of sustainable investments, particularly those focused on climate transition in public and private markets.- Integrating ESG factors into every investment decision, with special attention to climate change and transition prospects.- Establishing clear ESG expectations aligned with international standards and best practices, requiring all external investment managers, investee companies, and counterparties to comply.- Committed to reducing the Weighted Average Carbon Intensity (WACI) of the Exchange Fund's equity portfolio by 67% from 2017 levels by 2030 or earlier.Supporting Regional Transition through Investment- Continuing to engage with external investment managers to optimize investment opportunities that drive transition.- Continuing to identify and prioritize high-quality investment opportunities that promote Asian transition and generate positive global impact.First, maintaining a diversified and robust asset portfolio is crucial for achieving the primary investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe, potentially impacting investment returns and risk. Through an inclusive approach, the HKMA can seize opportunities to invest in companies undergoing transition that possess excellent technology and sound corporate governance to address evolving global climate trends, including those in high-emission industries.Second, addressing climate change requires the transformation of core "brown" industries. Merely excluding relevant investment projects or divesting does not help solve the problem of carbon emissions. Instead, the HKMA supports these industries by deploying strategic capital and exercising active ownership, driving their transition to sustainable and low-carbon operating practices, thereby creating beneficial shifts for both the industries themselves and the global community. The net-zero investment approach has evolved from a preference for green or low-carbon assets to encompassing assets with credible transition prospects, driving comprehensive carbon reduction across the entire economy. As a global asset owner, the HKMA understands that the long-term resilience of the asset portfolio depends not only on internal portfolio adjustments but also on broad economic transformation. Although there is no perfect single solution, the HKMA improved its responsible investment strategy in 2024, adopting a comprehensive and diversified approach to drive transition while supporting the net-zero goals of both the Exchange Fund and the global community. This strategy combines top-down and bottom-up tools, including integrating ESG factors into fundamental analysis and stewardship, tilting the portfolio toward carbon reduction, and making thematic investments in various assets aligned with the path to net-zero emissions. In public markets, this may involve tilting the portfolio toward ESG leaders or climate solution providers, coupled with stewardship to drive corporate transition. In private markets, the focus may be more on investment projects that facilitate transition. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the HKMA continues to identify investment opportunities that can promote climate transition while simultaneously enhancing the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund's asset portfolio.Sustainable investments across different asset classes account for over 10% of the Exchange Fund "portfolio," with financial performance comparable to the relevant portfolio benchmarks (Figure 5).- Public Market Investments: The HKMA has launched an active global equity portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition and has extended the application of customized low-carbon equity indices to two additional portfolios managed by external investment managers. The HKMA continues to seek Green, Social, and Sustainability (GSS) bonds that provide competitive returns while financing sustainable projects (see the case study in the section "Enhancing Sustainability through GSS Bonds").- Private Market Investments: The HKMA is committed to building a resilient long-term growth portfolio, seizing investment opportunities aligned with climate and energy transition themes. Leveraging its extensive network and expertise, the HKMA actively identifies and reviews investment opportunities that can accelerate the energy transition, including through strategic partnerships with cross-border organizations (see examples in the section "Jointly Addressing Climate Challenges from Asia to the World").- Passive portfolios using ESG indices as benchmarks.- Customized carbon reduction strategies for passive and active quantitative portfolios where the benchmark is not an ESG index.- Active portfolios with a governance theme.- Active ESG portfolios with a focus on sustainability and climate transition.- Projects with sustainable characteristics, such as renewable energy infrastructure, and buildings and warehouses with green certification.- Funds themed around energy transition and carbon reduction globally, in Asia, and in the Global South.- Green, Social, and Sustainability bonds.- A green bond fund managed by an international organization.- The "Multi-Currency Portfolio Management Program" (MCPP), managed by the International Finance Corporation, focusing on sustainable projects in emerging markets.- The "MCPP One Planet" project, providing climate-related investments in emerging markets that comply with the Paris Agreement.The HKMA invested in a green bond issued by a semi-official institution. The proceeds raised from the green bond were allocated to multiple projects, including upgrading aging equipment at several wastewater treatment facilities. These upgrade projects cover optimizing monitoring and control systems and pump performance to generate positive environmental benefits from wastewater management, waste reduction, and recycling processes. In addition to continuing wastewater and sludge treatment, these facilities compost or repurpose dehydrated sludge to produce fertilizers, charcoal, cement, and other construction materials, achieving a sludge recovery rate of up to 100%. These facilities also utilize gas generated during the sludge treatment process to power boilers and generate electricity.The HKMA invested in a green bond issued by a multilateral development bank. The bond finances multiple projects, including the restoration of a national canal system. As one of the country's largest irrigation systems, this canal aims to divert excess river water to arid regions. The primary objective of the project is to restore the increasingly deteriorating canal lining to prevent leakage, conserve water, improve water use efficiency, and reclaim waterlogged areas. Additionally, the project provides skills training for local stakeholders and promotes the adoption and effective use of modern irrigation technologies, such as micro-irrigation, and sustainable farming methods.

The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) is committed to becoming a responsible and sustainable institution. One of the key priorities for the HKMA in 2024 to fulfill this commitment is to accelerate its target date for achieving net-zero emissions from its institutional operations to 2030, twenty years ahead of the original target, in alignment with the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan." In addition to promoting environmental sustainability, the HKMA is committed to fostering staff training and well-being, advancing financial inclusion, and enhancing public financial literacy. The Green and Sustainability Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, serves as the primary decision-making body for all institutional sustainability measures. To demonstrate the HKMA's commitment to climate change, the Steering Committee approved in October 2024 the new target for the HKMA to achieve net-zero emissions from its institutional operations by or before 2030 as part of the "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" (the "Action Plan"). At the departmental level, the Assistant Chief Executive (Institutional Development and Operations) provides guidance on implementing sustainability measures related to institutional operations, staff well-being, and social engagement, and reports regularly to the Steering Committee. The Administration Group acts as the coordinator and central hub for executing, communicating, and reporting on institutional sustainability measures. The Green Office Task Force and the Volunteer Service Group, composed of staff from various operational departments, provide another layer of support; the former serves as a platform for brainstorming suggestions on creating a green working environment, while the latter aims to cultivate a culture of staff participation in volunteer activities. In recognition of the HKMA's dedication to caring for the environment, its staff, and society at large, the Hong Kong Federation of Youth Societies has awarded the HKMA the "15+ Caring Partnership" mark for 18 consecutive years from 2006 to 2024. The HKMA's sustainability strategy continues to be structured around three pillars: environment, staff, and social responsibility.- Focusing on carbon reduction and digitalization in the HKMA's daily operations, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by or before 2030.- Adopting green procurement requirements in accordance with government guidelines.- Promoting more environmentally friendly operational practices to the financial industry and the wider society.- Building a proactive workforce and talent pool to achieve the HKMA's strategic objectives.- Fostering a collaborative and caring working environment that values diversity and strengthens staff belonging.- Providing a high-quality working environment that promotes a healthy lifestyle.- Cultivating a culture of caring for society.- Incorporating social considerations into procurement procedures and supply chain management.- Promoting financial inclusion and enhancing public financial literacy through consumer education activities.The HKMA is concerned about climate change and leads by example. In October 2024, the HKMA announced its plan to accelerate the target date for achieving net-zero emissions from its own institutional operations to 2030, twenty years ahead of its original commitment, as part of the "Action Plan." The HKMA has revised its roadmap towards a net-zero transition, focusing on responsibly managing the environmental impact of daily operations, with an emphasis on reducing carbon emissions, energy conservation, paper reduction, and waste recycling, while fully leveraging improvements in the fuel mix for power generation by local utilities. Furthermore, the HKMA has established a digitalized working environment to improve efficiency while simultaneously reducing its carbon footprint. Additionally, recognizing the importance of cultivating a sustainability culture, the HKMA encourages staff to actively adopt practices conducive to sustainability through continuous promotional programs and activities. Under the primary net-zero emissions target for 2030, the HKMA has been exploring the adoption of carbon-embedded tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions and pursuing low-carbon procurement wherever possible. In this regard, since 2023, the HKMA has fully offset carbon emissions from air travel through the purchase of sustainable aviation fuel and participation in carbon offset schemes. The HKMA will expand its carbon-embedded and carbon offset programs to cover all other major carbon emissions. In addition to the aforementioned environmental commitments regarding actual operations, the HKMA continues to drive the market's low-carbon transition, from launching electronic document submission and processing procedures to promoting electronic payments and collecting coins for return to circulation. The remainder of this chapter details the HKMA's strategies in leading environmental protection, as well as promoting staff well-being and social care.Under the HKMA's overall institutional risk management framework, the Risk Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, is responsible for monitoring and reviewing potential risks and threats faced by the HKMA in its daily operations, including those arising from climate change. To more effectively assess the potential impact of climate change on operations, the HKMA has identified various climate-related risks and examined their actual and potential impacts. To address climate-related risks while ensuring business continuity, HKMA offices have been designed with multiple measures to mitigate potential physical hazards, fires, and other emergencies. Furthermore, the HKMA regularly updates its contingency plans, incorporating comprehensive measures that cover not only office premises but also communication and computer facilities. The HKMA conducts regular evacuation and backup facility activation drills to ensure staff are always prepared to execute contingency measures. The HKMA also monitors transition risks it faces by tracking greenhouse gas emissions generated from its own operations, waste generation, as well as energy consumption and paper usage. The HKMA's latest climate targets are to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions from Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 emissions related to institutional operations by or before 2030. These targets were formulated with reference to the methodology of the "Science Based Targets initiative" (SBTi). The HKMA adopts the "Greenhouse Gas Protocol" to measure and report institutional emissions. Scope 1 emissions are direct emissions from gasoline vehicles. Given the nature of its operations, the HKMA's primary greenhouse gas emissions are indirect Scope 2 emissions resulting from electricity consumption generated by fossil fuels. As there is no data from individual suppliers, the HKMA adopts a conservative approach to estimate major Scope 3 emissions from purchased goods (including capital goods) and services. Other relevant Scope 3 emissions include waste sent to landfills and staff air travel and commuting. Detailed calculation results for 2023 and 2024 are included in the "Performance Summary" on page 50. The performance data disclosed by the HKMA has been independently verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency (HKQAA). The scope and criteria of the verification are set out in the "Verification Statement" attached at the end of this report.The HKMA leads by example, adhering to the same climate-related standards that it expects the banks it regulates and the financial system it supervises to follow. As a first step towards green mobility, the HKMA began replacing its gasoline vehicles with electric vehicles in 2024 and will continue this work in 2025 to achieve comprehensive green mobility. The HKMA continues to integrate environmental factors into the design, operation, and maintenance of its offices. Specifically, in the 2024 renovation projects, the HKMA reused existing furniture and decoration materials or traded in old items for new ones to reduce waste. To enhance overall energy efficiency, the HKMA regularly reviews energy consumption and conservation measures in offices and data centers. In the 2024 data center facility upgrade project, the HKMA adopted a modular Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) system, further optimizing the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of its BEAM Plus-certified data centers. This design allows for flexible capacity expansion, improves operational efficiency under partial load, and is equipped with advanced cooling technology and higher power density, helping to reduce overall energy consumption. The HKMA strengthens internal virtual collaboration through digital workspaces, coupled with streamlined workflows, effectively reducing paper usage. Additionally, by extending the usage period of mobile and desktop devices in accordance with manufacturers' software update cycles, the HKMA can prolong the safe usage period of these devices. To reduce waste generated in offices, the HKMA adheres to the "4R" principles: Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle, and conducts regular waste audits to help formulate targeted waste management strategies. Recycling bins for different materials are available at multiple convenient locations within HKMA offices. To improve recycling rates, the HKMA added recycling bins for drink cartons and plastic fruit nets in 2024. Furthermore, since November 2022, the HKMA has sent collected food waste to a waste-to-energy facility in Hong Kong. In May 2024, the HKMA participated in the Environmental Protection Department's "Event Waste Reduction Pledge," committing to take measures to reduce waste generated by various events. The HKMA continues to prioritize the procurement of goods that meet the environmental specifications of the government's "Environmental Procurement List," particularly electrical appliances and office consumables. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the HKMA encourages staff to plan trips carefully, such as combining multiple journeys when attending overseas events. At the institutional level, the HKMA has purchased sustainable aviation fuel since 2023, reducing annual air travel carbon emissions by approximately 10%. Additionally, the HKMA participates in the "Gold Standard" certified carbon offset scheme to offset remaining air travel carbon emissions; this scheme focuses on renewable energy production and electrification projects in emerging markets.In 2024, the HKMA organized various learning activities for staff, such as lectures and guided tours of waste-to-energy facilities, to enhance their understanding of environmental sustainability issues. From Earth Day on April 22, 2024, through the entire month of May, the HKMA held its first "HKMA Green Month" with the theme "Green Thinking, Green Living, Green Working." This was an excellent opportunity to demonstrate the HKMA's commitment and drive to practice environmental sustainability in its internal operations. The activities included a "Sustainability BINGO Scorecard" to encourage staff to practice green living, a "Save the Earth" quiz game, and an indoor plant care workshop featuring "Kokedama" from Japan; results of waste audits were shared, and best practices in recycling were introduced by community recycling center operators. To sustain the momentum of "Green Month," the HKMA launched a recycling campaign lasting approximately six months in October, highlighting responsible waste disposal and reminding staff that aggregating small changes in personal habits can significantly improve the overall recycling performance of the institution. One highlight of the campaign was the release of the "Green 'Fit' Action" short video, featuring senior staff sharing recycling tips. The campaign also launched a series of screensavers, eye-catching posters, intranet articles, and electronic reminders to encourage staff to actively reduce waste and increase recycling. At the end of 2024, the HKMA conducted a staff survey to gauge their understanding of sustainability and collect their opinions on proposed green office measures. The survey results will help formulate future sustainability training activities and waste management strategies.As Hong Kong's central banking institution, the HKMA views itself as a key player in driving change and is committed to leading the acceleration of the low-carbon transition, promoting sustainable operational practices in the financial industry and society at large. The HKMA has introduced various measures to enhance the efficiency of its external processes. Following the successful launch of the "Shared Data Submission Platform" in 2023, the HKMA expanded the platform's service scope in 2024 to cover non-bank institutions, such as stored value facility operators, to facilitate their submission of certain regulatory data. The purpose of expanding the platform's service scope is to further simplify the submission process for reporting institutions, provide a smoother experience for all users, and reinforce the HKMA's commitment to sustainability. Other new measures launched in 2024 include SurveyTool, which allows banks to respond to HKMA surveys via a simplified submission process, and an intelligent information and document management system, providing a central platform for users to perform advanced searches on bank-related documents.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency has conducted an independent verification of the environmental data ("Data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority ("HKMA"). The Data includes total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, paper consumption, non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), and GHG emissions from air travel for 2024, along with their respective intensities. Additionally, the Data encompasses Scope 3 GHG emissions from purchased goods and services, capital goods, fuel and energy-related activities, non-hazardous waste (including general waste sent to landfill and recyclable waste), and employee commuting for 2023 and 2024, together with their corresponding intensities. The HKMA's GHG emissions data have been prepared in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol (GHG Protocol), jointly developed by the World Resources Institute (WRI) and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development (WBCSD). The verification scope covers a total of six office and warehouse assets: five offices located at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) Swire Plaza, 4) Kowloon Trade Centre, and 5) International Commerce Centre, and one warehouse at 6) Lo Shing Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The purpose of the verification is to provide reasonable assurance regarding the accuracy and reliability of the Data and to confirm the adequacy of the HKMA's data collection mechanisms. Within the verification scope, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency reviewed representative Data and supporting evidence selected from the six assets. This verification was conducted in accordance with the International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), "Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information," issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification procedures were designed to form an opinion and conclusion to achieve a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process was determined based on the requirements of the GHG Protocol. It tested the completeness and accuracy of the Data by tracing selected sample Data to their sources, and also reviewed and performed reliability testing on the underlying procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal checks. The verification process also included validating the internal data collection and management mechanisms, conducting interviews with representatives responsible for preparing the Data, and verifying representative Data and information. Relevant raw Data and supporting evidence were also subject to detailed review during the verification process. The HKMA is responsible for the collection and reporting of the Data. Our verification work is absolutely independent and impartial. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency verification team did not participate in the Data preparation process. Based on the results of this verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance and concludes that: - The Data is substantially accurate and reliable; - The HKMA's overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Shen Siu Yan, Review Supervisor, Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency, March 2025.
